case_summary.text: IT/ILT : Where assessee-company itself provided IT enabled services, company outsourcing its activities could not be taken as comparable for computing arm's length price
Co. outsourcing significant part of its operations can't be a comparable for a Co. rendering IT enabled services

IT/ILT : Where ITES segment of a company was similar to that of assessee-company engaged in provision of IT enabled services to its AEs, but there was discrepancy in annual report and in information gathered under section 133(6), said company could not have been taken as comparable
IT/ILT: A company which outsourced its work to sub-vendors as against assessee carrying out its activities in-house, could not be selected as comparable

IT/ILT : Where assessee-company was rendering software development services to AE, a company which apart from earning income form software services, also earned income from 'Business process outsourcing services', which fell in realm of IT enabled services and there was no segmental information qua software services alone, said company could not be accepted as comparable
Co. which is outsourcing its major activities can't be chosen as comparable for Co. doing its business in-house
IT/ILT : A company which has outsourced most of its work to third party cannot be compared to a company carrying out work by itself
IT/ILT : Where assessee was providing ITES services to AE, a company which outsourced substantial portion of its work, was not acceptable as comparable
Co. outsourcing major portion of its business to third party couldn't be taken as comparable for ITES provider
IT/ILT: Company engaged in provision of ITES services carrying on business through its own employees would not be comparable to a company which had outsourced a significant part of its operations
IT/ILT: In case of assessee rendering ITES services to AE, a company which had outsourced its significant work to outside ventures, was not acceptable as comparable
IT/ILT: Where assessee-company was providing ITeS itself while comparable company outsourced significant part of its activities, they could not be compared

IT/ILT : Where assessee was providing BPO services to AEs and employees cost was 62 per cent of total cost of services, whereas in company selected as comparable employee cost was less than 2 per cent which indicated that most of work was outsourced, company was to be excluded from list of comparables
A Co. mainly outsourcing its work couldn’t be compared to a Co. rendering IT enabled services

IT/ILT: Where assessee was rendering software development services to AE, a company dealing with software testing, software development services and healthcare services about which no separate segmental data was available, could not be accepted as comparable
IT/ILT: Where assessee rendered ITES services to AE, a company which developed its own software and a company which outsourced its significant work, could not be accepted as comparables
IT/ILT : Where assessee was carrying out BPO services by itself, companies outsourcing such work could not be taken as comparables
IT/ILT : Where assessee was rendering ITES service to AE, company which outsourced major portion of its business, could not be accepted as comparable
Co. providing IT services to its AE couldn't be compared with a co. providing BPO services
IT/ILT: Company which outsources its work is not comparable for ALP determination with a company that does activity inhouse

IT/ILT: Where assessee, engaged in manufacturing cassia gum powder, rendered marketing support services to its AE, company involved in high end niche market segment of financial contents and company which outsourced its ITES to third party vendors, could not be accepted as valid comparables while determining ALP
Co. outsourcing its activities couldn't be compared with a Co. providing services of its own
Cos outsourcing BPO work can't be a comparable for an entity undertaking such services in-house

IT/ILT: Where assessee was rendering software development services to AE, a company earning revenue from three segments namely software services, software products and other services about which segmental information was not available, was not acceptable as comparable
Co. included in comparable as it provided services similar to assessee’s, with segmental info available: ITAT
IT/ILT-I: In case of assessee, rendering ITES services to its AE, a company which significantly outsourced its activities, could not be accepted as comparable
IT/ILT: Business model of comparable being of outsourcing its service being different from in-house business model of providing services, said company was not was a comparable

IT/ILT : For computing arm's length price, comparability is to be judged primarily by functional similarity of entities; an entity outsourcing services cannot be compared to one rendering in house services

IT/ILT: Where assessee was rendering technical support and maintenance services to its AE, a company engaged in various activities such as sale of software licence, software services, export, revenue from subscription etc. about which no segmental information was available, could not be accepted as comparable

IT/ILT : In case of assessee-company rendering it Enabled Services (ITES) to its AE, a company providing geospatial services and a company which outsourced substantial portion of its work, could not be accepted as comparables while determining ALP

IT/ILT: In case of assessee rendering ITES services to AE, a company which followed different business model as it outsourced its work to external vendors, was not acceptable as comparable

HEADNOTE: Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITES)) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Assessee was engaged in providing Information Technology enabled back office support service in nature of customized proprietary research and analytic support - On other hand, a company was providing agency services by way of outsourcing services to third party vendor and acting as an intermediary between final customer and vendor - It was also involved in diversified high end services like e-publishing, data digitalization and digital library services - Whether said company was to be excluded from list of comparables on account of functional dissimilarities - Held, yes [Para 15] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING: Where assessee was engaged in providing IT enabled back office support service in nature of customized proprietary research and analytic support, a company providing agency services by way of outsourcing services to third party vendor and involved in diversified high end services was to be excluded from list of comparables on account of functional dissimilarities  TRANSFER PRICING: Where a company adopted different business model since total employee cost to revenue from operations was 23.35 per cent whereas in case of assessee same was 46.74 per cent, said company could not be selected as comparable to assessee  TRANSFER PRICING: A company in whose case extraordinary event of amalgamation was concluded which distorted profitability thereby increasing margin of comparable, said company was to be excluded form list of comparables  TRANSFER PRICING: A company which had seen wide range of fluctuations in its margin and its financial data was not reliable since promoters were involved in fraud, said company was to be excluded from list of comparables  TRANSFER PRICING: A company engaged in both Information Technology and Information Technology enabled services, in absence of segmental data, was to be excluded form list of comparables of assessee providing information technology enabled back office services  TRANSFER PRICING: Where working capital adjustment was allowed in assessee's own case for subsequent years, there being no change in business model of assessee, same was to be granted to assessee in impugned year also, however, it needs verification at level of Assessing Officer/TPO, thus issue was to be restored to TPO

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparabilty factors - Employee cost filter) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Whether where a company adopted different business model since total employee cost to revenue from operations was 23.35 per cent whereas in case of assessee same was 46.74 per cent, said company could not be selected as comparable to assessee - Held, yes [Para 16] [In favour of assessee]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparabilty factors - Abnormal event) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Whether a company in whose case extraordinary event of amalgamation was concluded during year under consideration which distorted profitability thereby increasing margin of comparable, said company was to be excluded form list of comparables - Held, yes [Para 16] [In favour of assessee]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparability factors - Unreliable financial statement) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Assessee was engaged in providing Information technology enabled back office support service in nature of customized proprietary research and analytic support - It was found that a company selected by TPO had seen wide range of fluctuations in its margin and its financial data was not reliable since promoters were involved in fraud - Whether said company was to be excluded from list of comparables - Held, yes [Paras 16 and 17] [In favour of assessee]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparability factors - Segmental results) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Assessee was engaged in providing Information technology enabled back office support service in nature of customized proprietary research and analytic support - On other hand, a company was engaged in both Information Technology and Information Technology enabled services, however, no segmental data was available - Whether said company was to be excluded form list of comparables - Held, yes [Paras 16 and 17] [In favour of assessee]

HEADNOTE: Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2008-09 - During relevant year, assessee rendered IT enabled services to its AE - Whether in case of assessee, a company engaged in outsourcing its major activities could not be accepted as a valid comparable while determining ALP - Held, yes - Whether a company providing tailored process outsourcing and management services could not be accepted as valid comparable in case of assessee - Held, yes - Whether a company indulged into translation segmental business, was functionally dissimilar to assessee and thus was not acceptable as comparable for benchmarking and determining ALP - Held, yes [Paras 11,15 and 18] [Matter remanded]IT/ILT : In case of assessee, rendering IT enabled services to its AE, companies having functional dissimilarity such as rendering tailored process outsourcing and translation services were not acceptable as comparables while determining ALP

FACT: During relevant year, assessee rendered IT enabled services to its AE.

In transfer pricing proceedings, TPO rejected economic analysis undertaken by assessee for determination of ALP in connection with aforesaid transactions.

Thereupon, the TPO on basis of profit margin earned by his own set of comparables, made certain addition to assessee's ALP.

The DRP confirmed addition made by the TPO.

The assessee filed instant appeal raising objection to selection of three comparables by the TPO namely, Coral Hub Ltd., Eclerx Services Ltd. and Cosmic Global Ltd.

HELD: It is noted from records that the DRP in assessee's own case in assessment year 2009-10 has directed the TPO to delete Coral Hub Ltd. from the final set of comparable with the observation that this company is outsourcing its activity whereas the assessee does not outsource. Therefore, the business modal of the assessee is different. [Para 9]

Further in the case of Mercer Consulting (India) (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT [2014] 150 ITD 1/47 taxmann.com 84 (Delhi - Trib.) for assessment year 2009-10, held that the Coral Hub Ltd. was not includable in the list of comparable because of major outsourcing and therefore, the same was required to be excluded from the list of comparables for measuring arm's length price of the ITES segmental transactions. [Para 10]

In view of above, it is opined that the outsourcing charges, which constitute more than 90 per cent of the total operating cost of the Coral Hub Ltd., is a very important factor and the same having greater bearing on the profitability of the comparable. In this situation, the Coral Hub Ltd. cannot be considered as a suitable comparable for benchmarking of International transactions of the assessee in ITES segmental activities, because the factum of heavy outsourcing activity carried out by this company looses the tag of suitable comparability. Since, the facts of the present case are similar to the facts of assessment year 2009-10, wherein the DRP itself did not find the Coral Hub Ltd. as a suitable comparable in the assessee company, therefore, following the view taken by Tribunal Delhi 'I' Bench in the case of Mercer Consulting (India) (P.) Ltd. (supra) it is held that Coral Hub Ltd. deserves to be excluded from the final list of comparables. [Para 11]

Eclerx Services Ltd.

It is noted that the Eclerx Services Ltd. is engaged in providing data analytics and customized process to its host of global clients which also provides services to the banking, manufacturing, retail, travel and hospitability business entities. DRP has not disputed this fact that the ITES segmental solutions offered by it also include data analytics operation management, audit and reconciliation, metrics management and reporting services. Apparently, this company provides tailored process outsourcing and management services in addition to multitude of the data aggregation, and mining and maintenance services. From annual report available on record, it can be easily seen that it is not closed to the assessee ITES segmental services transaction which are impressed by the manual process ITES services. The conclusion of the DRP that no comparable can be excluded on the ground of abnormal margin if its functionally comparable to the tested party cannot be accepted because mergers/demergers bring exceptional financial result which make such company as unfit for comparison. In view of foregoing discussion, it is held that the Eclerx Services Ltd. is not a suitable comparable to the assessee company for assessment year 2008-09 due to high pitched financial result and the same deserve to be deleted from the final set of comparables. [Para 15]

Cosmic Global Ltd.

HEADNOTE: Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (TNM method) - Assessment year 2005-06 - Whether where because of extraordinary event of amalgamation during relevant assessment year, financial result of comparable company was combined result of two companies, company was to be excluded from list of comparables - Held, yes - Whether Infosys Technologies Ltd. being a big company in all respects including range of turnover is not a comparable to small companies which are captive service providers having considerably low turnover - Held, yes - Whether where assessee itself has selected a company as comparable, it cannot operate as an estoppel in raising objections with regard to comparability of company - Held, yes - Whether, if employee cost of a comparable company is in low range, then it has to be assumed that said company has outsourced its business activities to third party vendor and, hence, company cannot be treated as comparable where assessee has carried out entire operations by itself - Held, yes - Whether in view of a question mark on reputation of owner of comparable company, it would be unsafe to take result of that company as comparable - Held, yes [Paras 6 ] [Partly in favour of assessee]IT/ILT: Infosys Technologies Ltd. being a big company in all respects including range of turnover is not a comparable to small companies which are captive service providers being considerably low turnover  IT/ILT: Where assessee itself had selected a company as comparable, it cannot operate as an estoppel in raising objections with regard to comparability of company

FACT: The assessee-company was engaged in the business of software development services and ITES/BPO services. The assessee during the year under dispute provided such services only to its Associated Enterprise (AE). It had selected TNM Method as the most appropriate method and OP/TC as the profit level indicator for both the segments.

On reference, the TPO rejected the TP document of the assessee pointing out various defects and deficiencies. He undertook a search in the databases and computed the ALP of both the segments.

On the basis of transfer pricing adjustment computed by the TPO, the Assessing Officer passed the assessment order making certain additions.

The Commissioner (Appeals) dismissed the appeal of the assessee rejecting all its contentions.

The assessee objected to the following companies being treated as comparables in the software service segment:

(i)

Exensys Software Solutions Ltd.: The assessee submitted that not only the aforesaid company was involved in development of products but there was also an extraordinary event of merger during the relevant financial year.

(ii)

Thirdware Solutions Ltd.: The company was into development of product and involved in distribution activities. Therefore, it could not be treated as a comparable.

(iii)

Infosys Technologies Ltd.: The assessee contended that under no circumstances Infosys Technologies Ltd. could be treated as comparable to the assessee as it is a giant in the sector of software development and ITES having considerable brand value. The revenue, on the other hand, while strongly opposing contention of the assessee, submitted that the assessee itself in its own TP Study had selected Infosys Technologies Ltd. as a comparable.

The assessee had also sought exclusion of following comparable companies selected by the TPO in the ITES segment:

(i)

Vishal Information Technologies Ltd.: The company had outsourced a considerable part of its business to third party vendors. That was proved from the fact that only 2 per cent of the revenue was spent towards employee cost and there was huge vendor payment.

(ii)

Maple E Solutions Ltd.: The company could not be treated as comparable as the directors of the said company were found to be involved in fraud, hence financial results of the company could not be trusted as reliable.

(iii)

Wipro BPO Solutions Ltd.: WIPRO commands a premium in the pricing of its products and services due to goodwill, reputation and brand value. Therefore, it could not be compared to a risk mitigated captive service provider like the assessee.

HELD: Software Service Segment

(i)

Exensys Software Solutions Ltd.

The Tribunal in the case of Intoto software India (P.) Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2013] 35 taxmann.com 421/[2014] 146 ITD 360 (Hyd. - Trib.) has held that the fact that there is an amalgamation of two companies which has resulted in high operating margin, cannot be lost sight for. The Tribunal remanded the issue to the Assessing Officer/TPO for reconsideration and held that if it was found that there was an amalgamation during the relevant previous year and the financial result was the combined result of the two companies, then, the company is to be excluded from the list of comparables.

FACT: The assessee was engaged in providing IT Support (ITES), account reconciliation services etc. to 'MS' group entities/its Associated Enterprises (AEs). It selected 9 companies as comparables and computed the margin on the basis of two years and average margin.

The Transfer Pricing Officer (TPO) rejected one of the assessee's comparables and accepted the remaining 8 comparables. However, it carried out its own research and included 19 comparables.

In the instant appeal before the Tribunal, the assessee disputed the inclusion of 14 comparables.

HELD: Comparable Company Eclerx Services

The Mumbai Tribunal in Willis Processing Services (India) Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2017] 83 taxmann.com 198 on considering similar contentions excluded this comparable holding that it was providing high-end data analytics and customized process solution and was a leading Indian provider of KPO services, which substantially varies from a low end ITES service provider, while for the assessee was engaged in providing BPO services. Therefore, the aforesaid comparable was functionally different from the assessee-company, and as such could not be selected as a comparable. [Para 32]

Considering the decision of the Delhi High Court in Rampgreen Solutions (P.) Ltd. v. CIT [2015] 60 taxmann.com 355/234 Taxman 573/377 ITR 533 and that of the Tribunal in Willis Processing Services (India) Ltd. (supra), company Eclerx Services is to be excluded from the list of comparables. [Para 33]

Comparable Company Mold-Tek Technologies

The co-ordinate bench of the Tribunal in Willis Processing Services (India) (P.) Ltd. (supra) excluded company Mold-Tek Technologies holding that it is a KPO and cannot be compared as against the assessee which is providing BPO services, and as such being functionally different from the assessee. [Para 34]

The Delhi High Court in Pr. CIT v. Evalueserve.com (P.) Ltd. [IT Appeal No. 921 of 2017] also upheld the exclusion of the company Mold-Tek Technologies holding that it provides engineering design, detailing services, website design services etc. and cannot be compared with the assessee which provides back office research services in IT Sector. Considering the aforesaid decisions, the company Mold-Tek Technology is to be excluded from the list of comparables. [Para 35]

Comparable Company Accentia Technology

Considering the decision of the Tribunal in Willis Processing Services (India) Ltd. (supra), wherein it was held that this comparable company is engaged in developing software product and rendering medical transcription services and cannot be compared with the assessee engaged in providing back office support services. Further, extraordinary events took place during the year which has an impact on its financials. Therefore, this comparable is directed to be excluded. [Para 36]

Comparable Company I Services

FACT: The assessee provided back office support services and related IT enabled services (ITES) to its AE. The assessee was remunerated on cost plus 10 per cent mark up basis for the above services.

The assessee had benchmarked its ITES services by selecting 14 comparable companies and by adopting TNMM as most appropriate method with average OP/TC as PLI of 14.56 per cent and claimed its international transactions having operating margin at 12.31 per cent, at arms length price.

The TPO rejected the TP analysis of the assessee and carried out a fresh search. The TPO selected 13 comparable companies and computed the average PLI at 24 per cent and, accordingly, computed TP adjustment.

On appeal: the assessee was seeking exclusion of 6 companies from the set of comparables considered by the TPO.

HELD: Comparable Datamatics financial Services Ltd.

The Tribunal in Goldman Sachs Services (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT [2016] 63 taxmann.com 9 (Bang. - Trib.) had an occasion to consider an identical issue. He held that since RPT exceeds 25 per cent of the sales, said company be excluded.

As therefore the Assessing Officer /TPO is directed to exclude this company from the set of comparable. [Para 28]

Comparable Maple e-solutions Ltd.

It is apparent that the comparability of this company was examined in assessee's own case and it was found that this company cannot be rejected as comparable on the alleged objections of involvement of directors of this company in alleged fraud. By following the order of this Tribunal in assessee's own case, this issue is decided against the assessee and in favour of the revenue. [Para 32]

Comparable Acit C. Mehta Financial Services

As regards, the employee cost as well as outsourcing cost in case of this company, there is no dispute that this company is outsourcing part of its business and the cost of outsourcing is 24.75 per cent of the total cost. This company was earlier known as Nucleus Netsoft and GIS India Ltd. As per schedule 9 of the balance sheet, this company has reported operations which included IT enabled services and software development apart from portfolio management fee. Thus, this company derives its main income from the operations of the IT enabled and software development activities and there is no separate data of sub-segment IT enabled services and software development. Therefore, the composite data of income from IT enabled services and software development cannot be considered as comparable prices of the assessee's IT enabled services. Further this company is paying data process charges to the extent of 24.75 per cent which shows that this company is outsourcing its IT enabled services activity instead of carrying out its own. As per the notes to accounts, this company has also reported that the scheme of amalgamation of this company has been sanctioned by the Bombay High Court. Therefore, this company amalgamated with Nucleus Netsoft and GIS India Ltd. with effect from 1-4-2005. [Para 42]

Gold stone Infratech Ltd.

As regards Goldstone Infratech Ltd. seg the information under section 133(6), the auditor of this company has furnished the details of export sale of BPO segment which contradicts the claim of the assessee that this company fails the export revenue filter. Since the TPO has applied this information without inviting objections to the assessee, therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the case and in the interest of natural justice, this issue is set aside to the record of the Assessing Officer /TPO to reconsider the same after affording opportunity to the assessee for raising the objections against this company. [Para 43]

Comparable Apex Knowledge Solutions

HEADNOTE: II. FACT: The assessee was also engaged in providing ITES to its AE and during the relevant previous year, it earned revenue from its overseas AE.

The assessee selected 13 comparables with arithmetic mean of 14.04 per cent. The margin shown by the assessee being 15.65 per cent, the price charged to the AE for the international transaction was found to be within arm's length.

The Transfer Pricing Officer after perusing the transfer pricing study of the assessee, however, was of the view that some of the companies selected by the assessee were not appropriate comparables as they did not match the functional profile of the assessee on FAR analysis. Observing that certain filters applied by the assessee were not appropriate, the Assessing Officer applied fresh filters for selecting comparables and selected 22 comparables with margin of 27.53 against 15.65 of assessee.

He accordingly, made TP adjustment.

The DRP confirmed order passed by the TPO.

On appeal:

HELD: Comparable Mold Tek Technologies Ltd.

The Tribunal in Maersk Global Centres India (P.) Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2014] 147 ITD 83/43 taxmann.com 100 (Mum. - Trib) while specifically dealing with the comparability of the aforesaid company to a ITES provider, has held that since the company engaged in providing engineering design service which was a high end service in the nature of KPO, it cannot be treated as comparable. In view of the aforesaid decision, this company cannot be treated as comparable to the assessee. [Para 13]

Comparable eClerx Services Ltd.

As per the annual report of this company, it is noted that the company is engaged in offering solutions in the field of data analytics, operations management, audits and re-conciliation, matrics management and reporting services. In fact, the Delhi High Court in Rampgreen Solutions (P.) Ltd. v. CIT [2015] 377 ITR 533/234 Taxman 573/60 taxmann.com 355, has held that this company being a KPO service provider cannot be considered as a comparable to ITES companies. Therefore, respectfully following said view, eClerx Services Ltd. being functionally different, cannot be treated as comparable to the assessee.

Comparable Vishal Technologies Ltd.

No doubt, assessee in the transfer pricing study has selected this company as a comparable. It is also a fact either before the Transfer Pricing Officer or the DRP, assessee has not raised any specific objection in respect of the aforesaid company. Even then, assessee's objection cannot be overruled for that reason alone. When the Transfer Pricing Officer has rejected the transfer pricing analysis of the assessee the department cannot use it selectively to their advantage. Moreover, it appears from the facts and materials placed on record that this company is different from the assessee considering the fact that it outsources its ITES to third party vendors. In other words, this company does not carry out the ITES activities itself but gets it done through others. This is evident from low employee cost of the company. Compared to the aforesaid practice of this company, the assessee claims to have carried out the ITES activities all by itself, thereby, has incurred a comparatively higher employee cost.

The Assessing Officer/TPO is directed to examine this aspect by verifying the annual report of the company and other relevant documents and if assessee's claim of low employee cost of this company is found to be correct, this company should not be treated as comparable. [Para 61]

Comparable Accentia Technologies Ltd.

Comparability of this company for the very same assessment year came up for consideration before the Tribunal, in Symphony Marketing Solutions India (P.) Ltd. v. ITO [2013] 38 taxmann.com 55 (Bang - Trib), the excluded this company on the reasoning that extraordinary event which took place might have impacted the profitability. In view of the aforesaid, this company cannot be treated as comparable. [Para 64]

FACT: The assessee was a wholly owned subsidiary of AEII USA and was engaged in the provision of IT enabled services to its overseas group company. For benchmarking, its transaction it selected 16 comparables whose mean margin was 20.96 per cent using multiple year data and submitted that their international transactions were at arm's length.

On appeal before the coordinate bench the matter was set aside to the file of the TPO to grant an opportunity to the assessee by providing information obtained by the Assessing Officer/TPO under section 133 (6) and to consider the submission.

On appeal to the Tribunal, the assessee sought exclusion of 11 comparables from the comparability list

HELD: For deciding a comparability the only guideline is rule 10B(2) of the Income-tax Rules 1962 and it cannot be said that a comparable can be decided on the basis of judicial precedent unless that precedent lay down some guiding factors to interpret rule 10B(2). Merely because a company is held not to be comparable with another company, it cannot be said that it becomes incomparable with the whole world. Such an approach is not only fallacious but also against the provisions of the 1962 Rules. Each Comparable needs to be tested on its own strength and weakness for comparability study. On this basis, the challenge of the assessee to various comparables is being tested.[Para 19]

Vishal information technologies Ltd.

HEADNOTE: Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Res judicata/Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether where a company had outsourced considerable portion of its ITES business, it could not be compared to assessee carrying out entire operation by itself - Held, yes - Whether a company mainly engaged in providing high end services involving specialized knowledge and domain expertise in field of data analytics and data process solutions was not comparable with assessee-company which was mainly engaged in providing low end services to group concerns - Held, yes - Whether a company having substantial goodwill being a parent company providing high end management solutions in health care was not comparable to assessee a captive service provider - Held, yes - Whether a consistent profit making company could not be rejected on ground that it had incurred loss in a particular year as functional comparability had to be seen - Held, yes - Whether where a company had been included/excluded from list of comparables in earlier years, consistent with view taken in earlier years and there being no change in facts and circumstances in instant year, same had to be included/excluded in list of final comparables - Held, yes [Paras 10 to 16][In favour of assessee]IT/ILT: Where a company had been included/excluded from list of comparables in earlier years, consistent with view taken in earlier years and there being no change in facts and circumstances in instant year, same had to be included/excluded in list of final comparables

FACT: The assessee was a company incorporated in India. It was a wholly owned subsidiary of Maersk GSC.

The assessee-company was mainly engaged in providing back office support to its AEs, which related to processing, data entry, reconciliation of statements, audit of shipping documents such as bills of lading and other technical support services. It also provided IT enabled services such as process support, process optimization and technical support.

During the relevant year, the assessee had carried out, inter alia, the international transactions of providing IT enabled services to its Associated Enterprises and nature of such services was stated to be transaction processing, data entry, accounting and other support services.

In the TP study report submitted by the assessee, the assessee had chosen 13 comparables. The average OP/TC of such comparables worked out at 10.93 per cent and hence it was reported that assessee's margin was at arm's length.

However, the TPO rejected all the comparables selected by the assessee, except for one comparable namely, Cosmic Global Ltd. He, after detailed discussion had finally adopted 5 comparables with an average margin of 43.07 per cent.

The DRP upheld the comparables finally chosen by the TPO, after giving direction to the Assessing Officer for making certain adjustments.

On appeal to Tribunal the assessee mainly challenged 3 comparables selected by the TPO namely: (i) Coral Hubs Ltd. (Vishal Information Technology Ltd.) (ii) Eclerx Services Ltd. (iii) Accentia Technologies Ltd. and it also challenged the rejection of 2 comparable companies by the TPO i.e (i) Allsec Technologies Ltd. and (ii) R. International Ltd. (Segmental) which were selected by the assessee.

HELD: Coral Hubs Ltd.(Vishal Information Technology Ltd.)

This company has been subject matter of dispute in assessee's case, whether to be included as comparable or not, since earlier years. In assessment year 2005-06, the Tribunal has excluded the said comparable on the ground that this company has outsourced its considerable portion of its ITES business, whereas the assessee is carrying out entire operation by itself. Similarly in assessment year 2006-07 also the Tribunal has excluded the said comparable on similar ground. In assessment year 2008-09, DRP itself has directed the Assessing Officer not to include Coral Hubs as a comparable company, which fact has been noted by the Special Bench in assessee's own case. Thus, consistent with the view taken in the earlier years and there being no change in facts and circumstances in this year, the assessee's contention that the Coral Hubs Ltd. (Vishal Information Technologies Ltd.) has to be excluded from the list of final comparables was acceptable. Accordingly, Coral Hubs Ltd. is directed to be excluded.[Para 10]

Eclerx Services Ltd.

HEADNOTE: Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether a company indulged in high skill IT services is non-comparable to routine IT enabled service provider - Held, yes - Whether a company engaged in developing its own software products and rendering medical transcription services can be compared to ITES service provider - Held, no - Whether a company which has outsourced its services to third party cannot be comparable to ITES service provider who is rendering services by it own - Held, yes - Whether a company involved in diverse nature of services, in absence of segmental data for diversified service portfolio, can be compared to IT service provider - Held, no [Paras 19 to 23] [Partly in favour of assessee]IT/ILT : A company indulged in high skill IT services is non-comparable to routine IT Enabled service provider

FACT: The assessee-company was a subsidiary company of a US Company.

It had rendered IT Enabled Services (ITES), i.e., BPO services to its associated enterprises and claimed the same to be at arms length price.

The TPO carried out a search analysis and after applying certain filters, had determined the final set of comparables. After considering the average margin of the comparables at 30.24 per cent, the TPO determined the arm's length price of the said international transactions which resulted in T.P adjustment.

The DRP confirmed the said order.

On appeal, the assessee challenged the inclusion of five concerns by the TPO in the final set of comparables.

HELD: Comparable Accentia Technologies Ltd.

The assessee pointed out that the Tribunal in the case of PTC Software (India) (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT [2015] 67 SOT 138/[2014] 52 taxmann.com 351 (Pune - Trib.) has considered Accentia Technologies Ltd. as non-comparable. On ground that it was engaged in developing its own software products and was rendering medical transcription services.

The plea of the assessee is quite potent and is infact based on the discussion available in public domain in the form of annual financial statement of the said concern. Moreover, in the light of the abovesaid decision of the Tribunal, there was no reason to negate the plea raised by the assessee for exclusion of Accentia Technologies Ltd. from the final set of comparables. [Para 11]

Comparable Cross Domain Solutions Ltd.

In Dy. CIT v. Wills Processing Services (India) (P.) Ltd. [2014] 51 taxmann.com 459 (Mum. - Trib.) this company has been rejected by the DRP on the ground that it is indulged in high skill IT services which are not comparable to the routine IT Enabled services.

Following the aforesaid precedent, assessee's plea for exclusion of Crossdomain Solutions Ltd. from the final set of comparables is upheld [Para 15]

Comparable Cosmic Global Ltd.

In relation to the financial year under consideration, the business model in which Cosmic Global Ltd. has functioned is quite dissimilar to the business model of the assessee while carrying out the activity of an ITES provider. Moreover, none of the objections raised by the assessee have been met by the TPO on the basis of any cogent reasoning. On that count also, the plea of the assessee to exclude Cosmic Global Ltd. from the final set of comparables is justified. The objection of the TPO that the said concern was found comparable by the assessee in earlier year cannot be the sole basis to include the said concern in the list of comparables, [Para 19]

Comparable Eclerx Services Ltd.

The Tribunal in Capital IQ Information Systems (India) (P.) Ltd. v. Addl. CIT [2014] 49 taxmann.com 313 (Hyd.) has held that as seen from the Annual Report, the above company is involved in diverse nature of services and there was no segmental data for diversified service portfolio. Moreover this company should be considered as KPO and this company is not comparable to assessee's services. [Para 22]

Thus, the plea of the assessee that the said concern is functionally dissimilar to the assessee, has been wrongly rejected by the TPO. Even there is no cogent reasoning brought out by the revenue to assail assessee's plea for exclusion of Eclerx Services Ltd. from the final set of comparables. [Para 23]

Comparable Coral Hubs Ltd.

HEADNOTE: Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2007-08 - Assessee-company was rendering IT enabled support services to its AE - Whether where a company had spent more than 26 per cent of total cost of employees and job work charges simply on outsourcing, business model of said company being significantly different from that of assessee, which was not outsourcing any of its work, would render it non-comparable - Held, yes [Para 4] [In favour of assessee]IT : Where a company had spent more than 26% of total cost of employees and job work charges simply on outsourcing, business model of said company being significantly different from that of assessee, which was not outsourcing any of its work, would render it non-comparable

FACT: The assessee-company was engaged in providing Captive IT enabled support services to its associated enterprises (AEs). The assessee selected itself as the tested party and applied Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) as the most appropriate method.

The TPO made certain variations in the comparables chosen by the assessee. Applying the arm's length margin rate of 28.11 per cent of such comparables, the TPO worked out the ALP of the 'Provision of IT enabled services' and thus, proposed transfer pricing adjustment.

The Commissioner (Appeals) reduced the transfer pricing addition.

The only issue raised by the assessee is to plead for the exclusion of e-Clerx Services Ltd. from the final list of comparables drawn by the TPO.

HELD: Comparable Clerx Services Ltd.

It can be seen from the Annual Report of the company, that it paid outsourcing charges to the tune of Rs. 8 crore and odd in addition to payment of Salary and wages etc. to its staff, including director's remuneration, to the tune of Rs. 24.54 crore. This divulges that roughly 26 per cent of the activity carried out by this company has been outsourced. As against this, the assessee is doing the entire business at its own without there being any expenditure on outsourcing. This reveals a significant difference in the business model adopted by the assessee and e-Clerx Services Ltd. E-Clerx has also spent more than 26 per cent of the total cost of the employees and job work charges simply on outsourcing, business model of said company being significantly different from that of the assessee, which was not outsourcing any of its work the same renders it non-comparable. Therefore, this company be excluded from the final set of comparables. [Para 6]

HEADNOTE: Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arms length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether a company which has outsourced most of its work to third party can be compared to a company carrying out work by itself - Held, no - Whether a company is not a comparable for having extraordinary circumstances, i.e., amalgamation - Held, yes - Whether where a comparable company is operating in a different business model than that of assessee, it should be excluded from comparable list - Held, yes - Whether a company indulged in high skill IT services is not comparable to routine IT Enabled services - Held, yes [Para 9] [In favour of assessee]IT/ILT : A company which has outsourced most of its work to third party cannot be compared to a company carrying out work by itself

FACT: The assessee had provided e-learning and content management services (including IT enabled services) to its associated enterprises.

The TPO had applied the TNM Method to determine the margins of the comparables and after selecting the set of comparables had computed the PLI of the comparables at 30.56 per cent as against the PLI of the assessee at 15.36 per cent. The TPO, thus, proposed an adjustment to be made to the international transaction.

The DRP revised the determination of adjustment to be made under section 92CA(3) and, subsequently, the Assessing Officer re-worked the adjustment, and added the same to the income of the assessee.

The plea of the assessee was that the TPO had erred in including (i) Accentia Technologies Ltd.; (ii) Cross Domain Solutions Ltd.; (iii) Cosmic Global Ltd.; and, (iv) Coral Hub Ltd. in the comparable list.

HELD: Comparable Coral Hubs Ltd.

The Tribunal in assessee's own case for earlier assessment year has given a finding that Coral Hub Ltd. could not be selected as a comparable as it is outsourcing most of its work and, thus, it has to be excluded from the list whereas the assessee was carrying out the work by itself. [Para 9]

In view of abovesaid precedent, Coral Hub Ltd. is to be excluded from final set of comparables. [Para 12]

Comparable Accentia Technologies Ltd.

The Tribunal in PTC Software (India) (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT [2014] 52 taxmann.com 351/[2015] 67 SOT 138 (Pune) (URO) and BNY Mellon International Operations (India) (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT [2015] 55 taxmann.com 386 (Pune) and also in Capital IQ Information Systems (India) (P.) Ltd. v. Addl. CIT [2014] 49 taxmann.com 313 (Hyd.) had held that Accentia Technologies Ltd. is not a comparable in IT segment for having extraordinary circumstances i.e. amalgamation.

In view thereof, Accentia Technologies Ltd. is to be excluded from the final set of comparables. [Para 14]

Comparable Cosmic Global Ltd.

The Tribunal in assessee's, own case for earlier year had held that the said concern is operating in a different business model wherein much of its activities are outsourced whereas the business model of the assessee is different. [Para 10]

Since Cosmic Global Ltd. was operating in different business model than the assessee in the year under consideration also, the same needs to be excluded from the final set of comparables and, accordingly, the Assessing Officer was directed to exclude the same from the final set of comparables. [Para 18]

Comparable Cross Domain Ltd.

The Tribunal in assessment year 2008-09 held that the said concern was to be excluded from the final list of comparables by observing that the business of Crossdomain Solutions Ltd. ranged from high end KPO services, which is not comparable to routine low end IT enabled services and the aforesaid concern is liable to be excluded from the list of comparables. During the relevant year, the company is providing agency services by way of outsourcing the services to third party vendors and acting as an intermediary between the final customer and the vendor. ITO [IT Appeal No. 3856 (Delhi) of 2010, dated 4-11-2010, a Co-ordinate Bench has held that the case of the assessee was not comparable with Infosys, the reason being that the latter was giant in the area of development of software and it assumes all risks, leading to higher profit and on the other hand, the assessee was a captive unit of its parent company in the USA and it assumed only limited currency risk. Comparable company Infosys BPO

The assessee has also placed the annual report of Infosys BPO Ltd. for assessment year 2013-14. Rich industry experience held the company to understand the evolving needs of the clients better and provided them with the ability to offer appropriate solution across different industry verticals and horizontals, quickly. Further, it is stated that the company is committed to providing best-in-class services to both horizontal and vertical focus areas. The horizontal solutions comprises of sourcing and procurement, customer services, finance and accounting, legal process outsourcing, sales and fulfilment, analytics, business platform, business transformation services, human resources outsourcing, technology solution optimization. While vertical solution included financial services and insurance, manufacturing, energy utilities, communication and services, retail, consumer packaged goods, logistics and life sciences. On looking at the horizontal services, which comparable company provides it is apparent that on this ground itself the same is not comparable with the assessee-company. On looking the annual accounts, it is apparent that comparable company has contributed INR 50,000,000 towards brand building and advertisement expenditure. Admittedly the company does not have any goodwill which can impact the profitability of the price of the business of its services because the goodwill is recorded on amalgamation in the nature of purchase only. Based on the above analysis, it is apparent that Infosys BPO Ltd. has a huge brand backing of the Infosys group behind it which can definitely impact the revenue as well as the profitability of the comparable company, therefore in absence of any such assets available to the assessee-company, Infosys BPO Ltd. is required to be excluded from the comparability analysis of ITeS segment. The TPO proceeded to apply external TNMM to benchmark the said international transaction.

The DRP noted that the nature of services being performed in AE segment was totally different from nature of services in non-AE segment as well as no audited segments were being maintained and the assessee had created artificial segmentation and confirmed T.P.O's order.

On appeal: HELD: The nature of services rendered by the assessee to non-AEs broadly comprised of customer care and technical support, viz., payroll, recruitment, IT support etc. The business operations of the assessee are divided into various operational processes that it performs for its customers (AE's and non - AE's). While processes carried out for the AE and non-AE may differ, the fundamental functions performed by the assessee under each of these processes are the same and fall under the category of ITeS Industry. These aspects were never disputed by the TPO/AO at any stage. In fact, the TPO/AO simply stated that the nature of services performed in AE segment are totally different from nature of services in non-AE segment. But how the services are fundamentally different has not been demonstrated by the Assessing Officer. In fact, in broader context the services rendered to AE and non-AE were that of customer care and technical support, and thus, rejecting the internal TNMM on this ground was not valid as internal TNMM is the method which makes it easy to find comparable companies and reasonably determine the arm's length nature of related as well as unrelated transactions. Besides this the TPO/AO has also rejected internal TNMM on the ground that there were no audited segments maintained. But at the same time, the TPO/AO has not pointed out any discrepancy related to segmental analysis based on valid allocation keys furnished by the assessee in its TP study. Therefore, these two aspects cannot be valid for rejecting the internal TNMM. The DRP was not correct in considering the services/scope of work from the agreement entered into by the assessee with its AE for 'procurement of IT Services' and comparing the same with the back-end ITeS services provided by the assessee to AEs. In the present case, best suited method is internal TNMM. The financial data pertaining to internal segmentation is more reliable and accurate, as compared to financial data of external comparable companies, therefore, it will be appropriate to apply internal benchmarking analysis over external benchmarking analysis. The "OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises and Tax Administrations" highlight the preference of internal comparables over external comparables. In fact, the United Nations Practical Manual on Transfer Pricing for Developing Countries, released in 2013 (UN manual) also provides that TNMM is less dependent on product comparability because net margins are less influenced by differences in products and functions, as compared to other methods like CUP. Therefore, the TPO/AO is directed adopt internal TNMM for benchmarking provision of ITeS. [Para 10]

HELD: Comparable Vishal Information Technologies Ltd.

This company is, inter alia, engaged in e-publishing, which is an activity similar to the one done by the assessee. However, despite having functionally similarity to a greater extent, this company cannot be considered as comparable because of a different business model adopted by it. Its annual accounts for the year ending 31-3-2007 are available on record. It can be seen that 'Operating expenses' are to the tune of Rs. 17.35 crores out of which a sum of Rs. 13.12 crores is on account of 'Data entry charges & Vendor Payments'. In contrast, the assessee is providing majority of its activities in-house. It goes without saying that there is a marked difference in profitability when the services are outsourced or provided in-house. Similar view has been taken by the Tribunal in several cases removing Vishal Information Technologies Ltd. on the basis of such business model. Under such circumstances, the Tribunal consider Vishal Information Technologies Ltd. as not comparable and directed to eliminate it from the list of comparables. The view point of the authorities in forcefully including a company in the list of comparables simply on the ground that since the assessee initially voluntarily treated it as comparable, now it cannot resile, cannot be appreciated. The substance of the matter is to consider and decide the comparability of a company with the assessee on merits rather than harping on an inadvertent mistake committed by the assessee in this regard. If an assessee wrongly includes a company in the list of comparables and then puts up a case before the TPO that this company is, in fact, not comparable citing the reasons for its stand, the TPO is obliged to reject the contention under due process of law after successfully meeting with the objections so raised by the assessee. It cannot be a one sided wind blow. There can be no estoppel against the inclusion of correct companies in the tally of comparables. If one has to go strictly with the assessee's list of comparables by not accepting the contention for the exclusion of a particular company after proper evaluation, then, there ought to be complete acceptance of the assessee's version as regards the comparability of all other companies as well. There cannot be simultaneous approbate and reprobate. As the position is not so and TPO is fully empowered to examine and evaluate each and every company included by the assessee in its list of comparables from the angle of its actual comparability, in the like manner, the TPO should also examine the assessee's contention of incomparability of a company wrongly included by it in the list of comparables, if argued. [Para 13]

HELD: Comparable Cosmic Global Ltd.

The TPO considered Cosmic Global Ltd. as comparable with the assessee-company on entity level. The second reason for considering this company as incomparable on entity level is the business model adopted by it. It can be seen that this company has outsourced major activities in comparison with the assessee doing its business in-house. It goes without saying that these two business models, namely, outsourcing services and providing in-house services, cannot be compared with each other because of their inherent differences. HELD: The issue arising in instant appeal relates to selection of comparables for determining ALP. Each of the comparables is considered as under:—

Cosmic Global Ltd.

This company is also excluded by DRP for the following reasons: that the expenses on sub-contracting is to the extent of 41 per cent; which suggests a different working model, which may have significant effect on the margin and therefore, the company cannot be retained as comparable.

The web report placed indicates that this company is in market research and analysis and IT services which include software development and maintenance. There is no segmental information. Assessee-company rendered ITE services to its AEs only and, thus, it was a capitive service provider - Whether where a company was not only rendering a variety of services but it also owned significant intangibles, enjoying goodwill and brand value of group which gave it more bargaining power and advantageous position with regard to pricing compared to a captive service provider, said company could not be comparable to a routine ITE service provider - Held, yes [Para 108] [In favour of assessee] FACT: The assessee had entered into international transactions in two segments, viz., Information Technology Enabled Services (ITES) and Software Development Services (SDS). He observed that the assessee had benchmarked the international transaction by applying Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) as the most appropriate method with operating profit/operating cost (OP/OC) as the profit level indicator (PLI). He found that in the ITES segment, the assessee had selected 14 comparables with average margin of 14.91 per cent as against the margin shown by the assessee at the rate of 9.82 per cent. Since the margin shown by the assessee was within ±5 per cent of the average margin of the comparables, the assessee had treated the transaction in ITES segment to be at arm's length.

As regards SDS segment, the assessee had selected 16 companies as comparables with average PLI of 10.66 per cent. Since the PLI of the SDS segment shown by the assessee was within ±5 per cent of the comparables selected, the price charged for the international transaction was treated to be at arm's length.

The Transfer Pricing Officer, however, did not find the transfer pricing study report submitted by the assessee reliable due to various deficiencies pointed out in his order. After rejecting the transfer pricing study report, the Transfer Pricing Officer proceeded to benchmark the international transactions under both the segments independently. The Transfer Pricing Officer proposed his own set of comparables and after considering the submissions/objections of the assessee, he finally selected 22 comparables in the ITES segment with average PLI of 27.53 per cent against PLI of 9.62 per cent shown by the assessee. Accordingly, he made an adjustment to the price charged by the assessee. As regards software development services, the Assessing Officer after rejecting the transfer pricing study report proceeded to select comparables independently. Out of the 16 comparables selected by the assessee, the Transfer Pricing Officer retained seven while rejecting the rest of the comparables. The total comparables finally selected by the Transfer Pricing Officer was 17 with average PLI of 22.90 per cent. Since the assessee had shown the margin of 9.62 per cent, the Transfer Pricing Officer made an upward adjustment.

The assessee challenged the aforesaid addition before the DRP contesting them on various grounds, however, it did not get the desired result and in pursuance to the directions of the DRP, the Assessing Officer completed the final assessment order.

This does not appear to be a valid reason for eliminating this case from the list of comparables. On going through the Annual accounts of Cosmic Global Limited, it is found that its total revenue from operations are at Rs.7.37 crore divided into three segments, namely, Medical transcription and consultancy services at Rs.9.90 lakhs, Translation charges at Rs.6.99 crore and Accounts BPO at Rs.27.76 lakhs. The assessee has made out a case that outsourcing activity carried out by this company constitutes 57 per cent of total expenses.

When one is examining the results of this company from the Accounts BPO segment alone, there is no need to examine the position under other segments. The entire outsourcing is confined to Translation charges paid at Rs.3.00 crore, which is strictly in the realm of the Translation segment, revenues from which are to the tune of Rs.6.99 crore. If this segment of Translation is not under consideration for deciding as to whether this case is comparable or not, one cannot take recourse to the figures which are relevant for segments other than accounts BPO. Thus it is held that this case cannot be excluded on the strength of outsourcing activity, which is alien to the relevant segment. [Para 13.2]

However, this case is found to incomparable on the alternative argument advanced by the assessee to the effect that total revenue of the Accounts BPO segment of Cosmic Global Limited is very low at Rs.27.76 lakhs. A captive unit cannot be compared with a giant case. The assessee objected to inclusion of four cases in the list of comparables.

The first case was of D, wherein the assessee claimed that on including one major transaction towards 'Reimbursement of expenses', the percentage of transactions with related parties became much more than 25 per cent, being, the filter adopted by the TPO himself. Revenue refused to exclude said case on ground that, the assessee had itself included 'G' in its list of comparables.

The third case was of 'M', whose exclusion was sought by the assessee on ground of 'unreliability of data', as the reputation of the group, owning M, was under serious indictment. Assessee also referred to cases where 'M' had been directed to be excluded from list of comparables on above grounds.

The last case was of 'V', wherein the assessee contended that it was engaged in providing IT enabled services on its own, whereas 'V' was outsourcing such services for provision to its customers and, therefore, was not a comparable case. The revenue contended that the profit of an entity outsourcing its services was likely to be less than an entity rendering services at its own and, therefore, it should be allowed to remain in the list.

HELD: Regarding inclusion of 'D' in list of comparables

There is no force in the contention advanced by the revenue for the exclusion of transactions with 'D' towards 'reimbursement of expenses' from the overall transactions entered into by 'D' with its AEs. Section 92F(v) defines 'transaction' in the context of transfer pricing provisions to include an arrangement, understanding or action in concert whether or not it is formal or in writing or whether or not it is intended to be enforceable by legal proceeding. There is no reference to any transaction having necessarily including profit element or mark-up so as to fall within the definition of 'transaction' under Chapter X.

Since the TPO applied filter of having companies with less than 25 per cent related party transactions, it is not open to argue that the transactions of reimbursement of expenses duly reported by 'D' as an 'international transaction' within the meaning of section 92B should be ignored simply because they represent reimbursement of expenses. If the contention of the revenue that the reimbursement of expenses not involving profit element should not be construed as a transaction, is taken to a logical conclusion, it would mean that all such dealings will cease to be transactions for the purposes of Chapter X. Once these dealings are not considered as 'transactions', these will also cease to be international transactions, going out of the purview of section 92 itself. Such a viewpoint is contrary to the clear intention and the language of the relevant provisions.

Aggrieved by the draft order of assessment, the assessee filed its objections before the DRP.

Pursuant to the DRP's direction, the Assessing Officer completed the assessment under section 143(3) r.w.s. 144(13) wherein the assessee's income was determined at Rs. 9.55 crore after inclusion of the TP adjustment of Rs. 1,58,79.279.

In appeal, dispute regarding selection and rejection of certain comparables were raised.

HELD: Universal Print Systems Ltd. (Segment BPO)

On similar facts (i.e., company fails the employees cost filter and is functionally different), as in the case on hand a co-ordinate Bench of this Tribunal in the case of CGI Information Systems & Management Consultants (P.) Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2018] 94 taxmann.com 97 (Bang. - Trib.), also for assessment year 2012-13, has remanded the issue of comparability analysis at the segmental level to the file of the TPO for examination and verification wherein it was held that there appears to be no bar in the rule 10B to consider segmental data under TNMM because the comparison is of 'net profit margin realized by the enterprise from an international transaction' with the 'net profit realized from a comparable uncontrolled transaction'. Therefore comparison is of similar transaction. When segmental information is available and is not disputed, it cannot be argued that filters have to be applied at entity level. It cannot be argued that when the TPO himself applied the filters at the entity level he was not entitled to apply the filters at segmental level. If clear segmental information is available the filters can be applied at the segmental level in TNMM. Therefore, the objection with regard to this company failing the employee cost filter and service revenue filter was rightly rejected by the TPO and DRP. It is however seen that this company has four segments viz., Repro, Label Printing, Offset Printing and Pre-press BPO. Whether the label printing and offset printing segments supplement the functions performed in the Pre-press BPO segment has to be seen. We therefore set aside the order of the DRP in this regard and remand for fresh consideration by the TPO the comparability of this company. In terms of rule 10B(3) of the Rules the profit margins of Pre-Press BPO have to be adjusted taking into account the fact that two other segments supplement the pre-press BPO segment. If such adjustment cannot be reasonably or accurately made then this company has to be excluded from the list of comparable companies. The TPO for this purpose can use his powers under section 133(6) to get required details from this company. As far as the argument that this company fails functional comparability, that none of the objections raised by the assessee in this regard about lack of information about allied services performed by the pre-press BPO segment of this company and the break-up of the revenue from such allied services have been dealt with specifically by the TPO or DRP. Since the comparability of this company is being remanded to be TPO for consideration of adjustments as mentioned above, the objection with regarded to functional comparability should also be looked into by the TPO in the remand proceedings on the basis of materials which he may gather under section 133(6). The assessee should be given opportunity of being heard by the TPO before the issue is decided by the TPO.
