Held, yes [Para 10] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING : Where employee/personnel cost of selected company, as percentage of total cost and sales, was negligible compared to personnel cost of assessee as percentage of total cost and sales turnover and this aforesaid facts do establish that company does not undertake provision of services itself but outsources major part of work to third parties then, company cannot be held comparable to assessee who in contrast, provides ITeS on its own without outsourcing  TRANSFER PRICING : A company failing filters applied by TPO which included more than 75 per cent service income filter and less than 25 per cent related party transaction filter then, company cannot be held comparable to assessee and should be excluded from list of comparables  TRANSFER PRICING : When directors/promoters of selected company were involved in serious fraud earlier therefore, different Benches of Tribunal as well as different High Courts including Jurisdictional High Court have held that this company cannot be treated as comparable due to unreliability of its financials then following same company should be excluded from list of comparables  TRANSFER PRICING : A company who has various segments and ITeS segment which also includes income from software development services however, segmental details relating to aforesaid services are not available and even otherwise also, nature of services provided by this company is relating to GIS which is considered to be KPO services thus, company is functionally different from assessee

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparability factors - Employee cost filter) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Whether where percentage of outsourced business of selected company had been reported as 44.81 per cent in same assessment year whereas assessee claimed that ratio of outsourcing expenses to total expenses was 65.98 per cent, TPO should verify exact quantum of outsourcing expenses in case of selected company and decide issue of exclusion of said company in accordance with law and after giving adequate opportunity of being heard to assessee - Held, yes [Para 18] [Matter remanded]  II. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparability factors - Abnormal events) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Whether a company having extraordinary event such as merger/demerger could not be compared with assessee-company - Held, yes [Para 20.1] [In favour of assessee]  III. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITES)) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Whether where assessee sought to exclude a company as being functionally different but TPO had gathered financial and functional details of company by way of using his authority under section 133(6) and included said company as comparable but said information had not been provided to assessee, matter should be restored to file of Assessing Officer/TPO to decide issue afresh after furnishing information gathered under section 133(6) to assessee - Held, yes [Para 23] [Matter remanded]  IV. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparability factors - Unreliable financial statement) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Whether where data provided by selected company was unreliable due to fraud committed by owner/directors, then said company could not be held as comparable to assessee - Held, yes [Para 35] [In favour of assessee]  V. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITES)) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Whether where selected company was having only one segment of Information Technology enabled Services and was primarily engaged in field of IT-BPO, Assessing Officer/TPO should include company into set of comparables to assessee - Held, yes [Para 39.1] [In favour of assessee]

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITESs)) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether a company which is not purely in field of rendering ITES services and whose segmental results cannot be relied then, company cannot be held good comparable for assessee and should be excluded from list of comparable - Held, yes [Para 5.1] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING : A company which is not purely in field of rendering ITES services whose segmental results cannot be relied then company cannot be held good comparable for assessee and should be excluded from list of comparable  TRANSFER PRICING : When Co-ordinate Bench of High Court in similar instant in previous AY held that two entities could not be compared with each other as company has outsourced its services to outside vendors as against fact that assessee has rendered services itself, then following same company cannot be held comparable with assessee and should be excluded from list of comparable

I.Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961, read with rule 10B(2) of the Income-tax Rules, 1962 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2007-08 - Whether merely because a company is held not to be comparable with another company, it cannot be said that it becomes incomparable with whole world as each comparable needs to be tested on its own strength and weakness for comparability study - Held, yes - Assessee company was engaged in provision of ITES services to its overseas group company which were different from KPO - Whether assessee carrying on business through its own employees would not be comparable to a company which had outsourced a significant part of its operations - Held, yes - Whether a KPO company engaged in providing high-end engineering consulting services employing engineers to provide such services would not be comparable to assessee a BPO - Held, yes - Whether a company having extraordinary events of merger in absence of segmental information would not be functionally comparable - Held, yes - Whether in view of absence of segmental information a software developer would not be functionally comparable with a pure captive service provider - Held, yes - Whether a company having fluctuating profits would not be comparable - Held, yes - Whether without having concise and precise financial information about company for same financial period, it could not be taken as comparable - Held, yes - Whether a company having high gross revenue almost 1200 times of turnover of assessee-company would not be comparable - Held, yes - Whether where two companies were sought to be excluded on ground that their owners had committed a fraud and, therefore, financials of these companies could not be compared, in view of fact that fraud committed in earlier years did not have impact on financials of current years and revenue of both companies had increased in present year from last year, said two companies were to be retained - Held, yes [Paras 19, 33, 36, 40, 43, 47, 50, 53, 57, 60  64][Partly in favour of assessee]IT/ILT: Company engaged in provision of ITES services carrying on business through its own employees would not be comparable to a company which had outsourced a significant part of its operations  IT/ILT: Foreign exchange gain or loss is part of operating expenditure/ income

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Assessee rendered ITE services to its AE - Whether a company providing medical transaction, billing and coding services and application development and customization service in respect of which segmental data was not available was incomparable - Held, yes [Para 3][In favour of assessee]IT/ILT: A company providing medical transaction, billing and coding services, application development and customization service in respect of which segmental data was not available, was incomparable to ITES provider  IT/ILT: Extraordinary events such as merger/amalgamation would have an impact/effect on profitability of a comparable company and would oust said company from comparability analysis  IT/ILT: A company which outsourced its work to sub-vendors as against assessee carrying out its activities in-house, could not be selected as comparable  IT/ILT: A company engaged in 'knowledge Process Outsourcing' (KPO) service, development of products and routine IT services was incomparable to ITES provider

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Assessee-company was a routine ITeS i.e. low-end service provider to its AEs - Whether it would not be a suitable comparable with a high-end KPO company providing data analytics and data process solutions to global enterprise clients having significant intangibles and also providing sales and marketing support services to leading global manufacturing, retail, travel and leisure companies through its pricing and profitability service - Held, yes [Paras 7.8  7.13][In favour of assessee]IT/ILT : High-end KPO company providing data analytics and data process solutions to global enterprise clients having significant intangibles would not be comparable to a routine low-end ITeS provider   IT/ILT : Company engaged in providing both software development services as well as IT enabled Services, in view of substantial activity of software development and in absence of segmental data would not be comparable to a routine low-end ITeS provider   IT/ILT : Company which had outsourced most of its work would not be comparable to assessee which carried out its work by itself by recruiting employees  IT/ILT : Activity of consultancy in structural engineering cannot be compared with routine services of coordination, administrative support and other IT enabled support services rendered by assessee to its AE  IT/ILT : Grant of working capital adjustment could not have been restricted only in case of manufacturers or traders as what is true for these categories of businesses, is fully true for service providers as well

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparability factors - Employee cost filter) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Whether where percentage of outsourced business of selected company had been reported as 44.81 per cent in same assessment year whereas assessee claimed that ratio of outsourcing expenses to total expenses was 65.98 per cent, TPO should verify exact quantum of outsourcing expenses in case of selected company and decide issue of exclusion of said company in accordance with law and after giving adequate opportunity of being heard to assessee - Held, yes [Para 18] [Matter remanded]TRANSFER PRICING : Where percentage of outsourced business of selected company had been reported as 44.81 per cent in same AY whereas assessee claimed that ratio of outsourcing expenses to total expenses was 65.98 per cent, TPO should verify exact quantum of outsourcing expenses in case of selected company and decide exclusion of comparable company in accordance with law and after giving adequate opportunity of being heard to assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : A company having extraordinary event such as merger/demerger could not be compared with assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : When assessee sought to exclude company as being functionally different but TPO had gathered financial and functional details of company by way of using his authority under section 133(6) and included said company as comparable but said information had not been provided to assessee, matter should be restored to file of AO/TPO to decide issue afresh  TRANSFER PRICING : Where data provided by selected company was unreliable due to fraud committed by owner/directors, then said company cannot be held as comparables to assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : Where selected company was having only one segment of Information Technology enabled services and was primarily engaged in field of IT-BPO, AO/TPO should include said company into set of comparables to assessee ITES provider

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arms length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether a company which has outsourced most of its work to third party can be compared to a company carrying out work by itself - Held, no - Whether a company is not a comparable for having extraordinary circumstances, i.e., amalgamation - Held, yes - Whether where a comparable company is operating in a different business model than that of assessee, it should be excluded from comparable list - Held, yes - Whether a company indulged in high skill IT services is not comparable to routine IT Enabled services - Held, yes [Para 9] [In favour of assessee]IT/ILT : A company which has outsourced most of its work to third party cannot be compared to a company carrying out work by itself

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2007-08 - Assessee company a wholly owned subsidiary of a US company engaged into providing Information Technology (IT) Enabled Back Office support services relating to creation and maintenance of database of prospective employers -Whether a company in whose case extraordinary event of amalgamation had taken place during relevant year, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes - Whether where there was wide gap between employee cost of assessee vis-à-vis comparable company it could not be taken as valid comparable - Held, yes -Whether annual report is to be relied upon as against information under section 133(6), thus where there was contradiction in information supplied under section 133(6) stating activities of comparable to be in form of ITES whereas in annual report it was categorically mentioned that said comparable had only one segment i.e software development, it could not be taken as comparable - Held, yes - Whether a knowledge process outsourcing company engaged in providing consulting services, process outsourcing, process re-engineering and automation services, would not be a valid comparable for benchmarking international transaction qua ITES services undertaken by assessee - Held, yes - Whether companies having less than 25 per cent of sales as employee cost should not be chosen for comparability and hence had to be excluded - Held, yes - Whether a full-fledged risk taking company having diversifying business owning significant intangibles would not be comparable to assessee a minimal risk taking company having no intangibles- Held, yes - Whether company which had outsourced most of its services to other vendors/service providers would not be comparable to assessee being a captive provider engaged in back office work - Held, yes [Paras 17, 19, 22, 27, 32, 34, 37  40 ][Partly in favour of assessee]IT/ILT: A full-fledged risk taking company having diversifying business and owning significant intangibles would not be comparable to assessee a minimal risk taking company providing Information Technology (IT) Enabled Back Office support services and having no intangibles

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Assessee-company was rendering IT enabled back office services to its AE - In transfer pricing proceedings, assessee raised objection to selection of one comparable in final list of comparables - It was noted that said comparable was outsourcing its agency services because it had a wages/sales ratio of 1.25 per cent as compared to assessee's wages/sales ratio of 53 per cent - Moreover, apart from providing IT enabled services, said comparable was rendering technical services as well e.g. e-publishing services and, thus, there existed functional difference - Whether, on facts, Assessing Officer was to be directed to exclude company objected to by assessee from list of comparables - Held, yes [Paras 16, 20 and 30] [In favour of assessee]IT/ILT : In case of assessee, rendering IT enabled back office services to its AE, a company outsourcing its agency services could not be accepted as valid comparable while determining ALP

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2005-06 - Assessee company was engaged in providing back office support services to its AE, its services mainly came under BPO services - Whether a company engaged in software development services would not be comparable to assessee - Held, yes - Whether where a company had outsourced considerable portion of its business, and employee cost of this company was very low as compared to assessee, it could not be taken as comparable to assessee carrying out entire operation by itself - Held, yes - Whether a company having very high turnover could not be selected as comparable - Held, yes - Whether where one of filters applied by TPO to select / reject comparable was RPT of more than 25 per cent, company having RPT of more than 25 per cent should not be treated as a comparable to assessee - Held, yes - Whether where financial results of company were not reliable due to fraud committed by directors, certainly it should not be considered for comparability analysis - Held, yes - Whether where TPO rejected a company on grounds that it had not earned any export revenue, however same could not be verified due to insufficiency of information, matter required readjudictaion - Held, yes - Whether where on perusal of annual report of company, it was evident that company was into ITES/BPO service like assessee, issue relating to comparability was to be remitted back to TPO to ascertain functional profile of company along with assets employed and risk undertaken in detail for coming to a conclusion as to whether this company was comparable to assessee - Held, yes [Paras 6, 9, 13, 16, 20, 23, 27  30] [In favour of assessee/Matter remanded]IT/ILT: Where a company had outsourced major portion of its business activities and employee cost of this company was very low as compared to assessee, it would not be comparable to assessee carrying out entire operation by itself  IT/ILT: Where assessee in its TP study claimed risk adjustment and TPO also observed that assessee appeared to bear some amount of risk, such as, single customer risk, but, rejected claim of assessee on ground that assessee had not properly quantified risk adjustment, matter was to be remanded back for disposal afresh

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparable and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2010-11 - Assessee-company was engaged in provision of software development services to its AE - Whether a company engaged in both software development and ITES in absence of segmental data was not comparable to assessee - Held, yes - Whether fluctuating profits could not be a reason to exclude companies unless business profile was entirely different - Held, yes - Whether where assessee objected to a company on ground that it outsourced its business, there was presence of intangible assets and also said company had very high turnover, Assessing Officer/TPO not having examined matter, it was to be remitted back for fresh adjudication by Assessing Officer/TPO to see whether functional dissimilarity and high turnover had application to facts of case of assessee-company - Held, yes [Partly in favour of assessee]IT/ILT: Company engaged in both software development and ITES in absence of segmental data is not comparable to company engaged only in software development services  IT/ILT: Where bad debts and provision for bad and doubtful debts were part of operating expenses, TPO was to be directed to re-compute margins of comparable companies by including them for purpose of computing profit and loss of comparable companies  IT/ILT: There is no need for making any negative working capital adjustment when assessee does not bear any working capital risk

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITESs)) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether a company which is not purely in field of rendering ITES services and whose segmental results cannot be relied then, company cannot be held good comparable for assessee and should be excluded from list of comparable - Held, yes [Para 5.1] [In favour of assessee]  II. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparability factors - Employee cost filter) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether where Co-ordinate Bench of High Court in similar instant in previous assessment year held that two entities could not be compared with each other as company has outsourced its services to outside vendors as against fact that assessee has rendered services itself, then following same company cannot be held comparable with assessee and should be excluded from list of comparable - Held, yes [Para 5.2] [In favour of assessee]

II. Section  92C  of the Income-tax Act, 1961 -  Transfer pricing  -  Computation of arm’s length price  (Comparables - Functional Similarity-Information Technology Enabled Services (ITES)) - Assessment year  2020-21  - Whether a company engaged in accounting, auditing and bookkeeping services could not be considered as a valid comparable for assessee rendering routine ITES/DCM services - Held, yes - Whether further lack of reliable segmental information to carve out margins relating to comparable services would further disqualify said company from being considered as valid comparable - Held, yes [Para 36.1] [In favour of assessee]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Assessee-company was engaged in rendering software development services and IT enabled services to its AE - Whether where a company had outsourced considerable portion of its ITES business, it could not be compared to assessee carrying out entire operation by itself - Held, yes - Whether a company mainly engaged in providing high end services involving specialized knowledge and domain expertise in field of data analytics and data process solutions was not comparable to assessee - Held,yes [Paras 22 and 23] [In favour of assessee/Matter remanded]

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2007-08 - Assessee-company was providing IT enabled services (ITES) to its AE - Whether a company in whose case extraordinary event of amalgamation took place during relevant year which affected its financial results, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes - Whether a company which outsourced major part of its work resulting in very low employee cost, was also not acceptable as comparable - Held, yes - Whether a company earning revenue from sale of its own software products, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes - Whether a company engaged in rendering KPO services was also not acceptable as comparable - Held, yes - Whether a company providing highly technical engineering consultancy services was to be rejected as comparable on account of functional difference - Held, yes [Para 10.4] [Matter remanded]IT/ILT : In case of assessee-company providing IT enabled services [ITES] to its AE, a company which outsourced major part of its work, company earning revenue from sale of its own software products, a company engaged in rendering KPO services, and a company providing highly technical engineering consultancy services, could not be accepted as comparables while determining ALP  IT/ILT : Matter relating to working capital adjustment was to be remanded back for disposal afresh with a direction that in case said working capital adjustment came to negative, no such adjustment was required to be made

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2009-10 - Whether a company mainly outsourcing its activities cannot be compared to ITES service provider mainly rendering services by its own - Held, yes - Whether a company engaged in providing full range of geospatial services cannot be compared to a company rendering ITES services - Held, yes - Whether extraordinary events like mergers and acquisitions are sufficient enough to justify its exclusion from list of comparables - Held, yes - Whether a KPO company cannot be compared to an ITES service providers mainly rendering services to its AE - Held, yes - Whether an incomparable company cannot per se be included in final set of comparables simply for reason that assessee inadvertently so included it initially - Held, yes [Paras 9 to 38] [In favour of assessee/Matter remanded]IT/ILT : A company mainly outsourcing its activities cannot be compared to ITES service provider rendering services by its own

II. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Assessee rendered ITES to its AE - Whether company engaged in providing engineering design service which is a high end service in nature of KPO,cannot be treated as comparable - Held, yes - Whether company which had outsourced its ITES to third party vendors was incomparable - Held, yes - Whether since extraordinary event had impacted profitability of comparable company, it should be excluded from comparable list - Held, yes - Whether engineering design services could not be compared to IT enabled services - Held, yes [Paras 53 to 67][Matter remanded]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables and adjustment/Compareable - Illustration) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Assessee was engaged in business of software development Service to its AE - Whether when comparable company had outsourced its ITES services, should be excluded from comparable list - Held, yes - Whether company engaged in KPO services could not be compared with low end service provider - Held, yes - Whether extraordinary event of amalgamation during year had helped comparable in acquiring domains skill sets in finance, administration space as well as enhanced its global presence and, therefore, it excluded from list of comparables - Held yes - Whether in absence of Director's Report and Notes to Account of comparable in public domain, it would not be prudent to take this company as a comparable - Held, yes - Whether a company which was into mapping business and was providing geographical information services, could not be said to be comparable - Held, yes - Whether a software development service provider in absence of segmental information, could be selected as comparable - Held, no [Paras 8-34] [Partly in favour of assessee]

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2011-12 - Assessee-company was providing IT enabled services (ITES) to its AE - Whether a company engaged in rendering high end KPO services, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes - Whether a company rendering engineering design services was not acceptable as comparable - Held, yes - Whether a company which outsourced major portion of its work and, thus, followed a different business model, was unacceptable as comparable - Held, yes - Whether a company engaged in various IT services including software development and maintenance, was not acceptable as comparable - Held, yes - Whether a company providing technical services such as software testing, verification and validation of software, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes [Paras 11.2 to 29.2] [Matter remanded]IT/ILT : In case of assessee-company rendering IT enabled services (ITES) to its AE, a company engaged in rendering high end KPO services, a company rendering engineering design services, a company which outsourced major portion of its work and a company providing technical services such as software testing, verification and validation of software, could not be accepted as comparables while determining ALP

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2008-09 - During relevant year, assessee rendered IT enabled services to its AE - Whether in case of assessee, a company engaged in outsourcing its major activities could not be accepted as a valid comparable while determining ALP - Held, yes - Whether a company providing tailored process outsourcing and management services could not be accepted as valid comparable in case of assessee - Held, yes - Whether a company indulged into translation segmental business, was functionally dissimilar to assessee and thus was not acceptable as comparable for benchmarking and determining ALP - Held, yes [Paras 11,15 and 18] [Matter remanded]IT/ILT : In case of assessee, rendering IT enabled services to its AE, companies having functional dissimilarity such as rendering tailored process outsourcing and translation services were not acceptable as comparables while determining ALP

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITES)) - Assessment year 2006-07 - Assessee was engaged in providing Information Technology enabled back office support service in nature of customized proprietary research and analytic support - On other hand, a company was providing agency services by way of outsourcing services to third party vendor and acting as an intermediary between final customer and vendor - It was also involved in diversified high end services like e-publishing, data digitalization and digital library services - Whether said company was to be excluded from list of comparables on account of functional dissimilarities - Held, yes [Para 15] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING: Where assessee was engaged in providing IT enabled back office support service in nature of customized proprietary research and analytic support, a company providing agency services by way of outsourcing services to third party vendor and involved in diversified high end services was to be excluded from list of comparables on account of functional dissimilarities  TRANSFER PRICING: Where a company adopted different business model since total employee cost to revenue from operations was 23.35 per cent whereas in case of assessee same was 46.74 per cent, said company could not be selected as comparable to assessee  TRANSFER PRICING: A company in whose case extraordinary event of amalgamation was concluded which distorted profitability thereby increasing margin of comparable, said company was to be excluded form list of comparables  TRANSFER PRICING: A company which had seen wide range of fluctuations in its margin and its financial data was not reliable since promoters were involved in fraud, said company was to be excluded from list of comparables  TRANSFER PRICING: A company engaged in both Information Technology and Information Technology enabled services, in absence of segmental data, was to be excluded form list of comparables of assessee providing information technology enabled back office services  TRANSFER PRICING: Where working capital adjustment was allowed in assessee's own case for subsequent years, there being no change in business model of assessee, same was to be granted to assessee in impugned year also, however, it needs verification at level of Assessing Officer/TPO, thus issue was to be restored to TPO

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2007-08 - Assessee was engaged in manufacturing guar gum and cassia gum powder - During relevant year, assessee was rendering marketing support services to its AE - Whether a company involved in high end niche market segment of financial contents, could not be compared with routine marketing support services in which assessee was involved - Held, yes - Whether a company whose directors were facing charges of fraud and thus its financial results were not reliable, could not be accepted as valid comparable - Held, yes - Whether a company which had outsourced its ITES services to third party vendors, could not be accepted as valid comparable while determining ALP - Held, yes - Whether a company in whose case there was disproportionate fluctuation in rate of operating profit in earlier years due to extra-ordinary reasons like merger, could not be regarded as valid comparable - Held, yes [Paras 17 to 23] [Matter remanded]IT/ILT: Where assessee, engaged in manufacturing cassia gum powder, rendered marketing support services to its AE, company involved in high end niche market segment of financial contents and company which outsourced its ITES to third party vendors, could not be accepted as valid comparables while determining ALP

II. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2007-08 - During relevant year, assessee-company was rendering IT enabled services (ITES) to its AE - Held that a company rendering high end KPO services, could not be accepted as comparable while determining ALP - Companies having related party transactions in excess of 15 per cent of revenue, were not acceptable as comparables - Companies which outsourced substantial part of their work could not be compared with low end service provider like assessee - Further, companies which were tainted because of involvement in financial and economic irregularities were not acceptable as comparables - A company in whose case extraordinary event of merger a took placed during relevant year, was not acceptable as comparable - Company engaged in business of rendering engineering services in nature of producing design, drawings, detailed structural engineering drawings using 3D and 2D software, was also unacceptable as comparable on account of functional difference [Para 12] [Matter remanded]

II. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables and adjustments/Comparables - Illustrations) - Assessment year 2010-11 - During relevant year, assessee-company was rendering IT enabled services (ITES) to its AE - Whether a company in whose case extraordinary event of amalgamation took place, was not acceptable as valid comparable while determining ALP - Held, yes - Whether a company rendering technical services such as software testing, verification and validation of software item, implementation and data centre management activities, could not be accepted as comparable - Held, yes - Whether a company rendering ITES services after outsourcing same to third parties, could not be considered as comparable to assessee-company which was rendering exclusively in-house services - Held, yes [Paras 27.2 to 37] [Matter remanded]

I. Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITESs)) - Assessment year 2004-05 - Whether since assessee has itself selected company as a comparable company in its TP study and selected company was also in ITES services which could be separated or segmented, like in assessee's case also could not be verified therefore, comparability of selected company is required to be reexamined by TPO - Held, yes [Para 16.5] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING : Where assessee has itself selected company as a comparable company in its TP study and selected company was also in ITES services which could be separated or segmented, like in assessee's case also could not be verified therefore, comparability of selected company is required to be re-examined by TPO  TRANSFER PRICING : Both loss making unit and high profit making unit cannot be eliminated from comparables unless, there are specific reasons for eliminating same which is other than general reason that comparable has incurred loss or made abnormal profits  TRANSFER PRICING : A company who has developed unique software from which it would derive substantial benefits advantages when compared with assessee which is undertaking pure call centre services therefore, company cannot be held as comparable to assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : A company who is outsourcing most of its work cannot be held comparable to assessee who was carrying out work by itself  TRANSFER PRICING : A company who having influence of 'Wipro' brand and also having its unique intangibles cannot be held comparable to captive service provider such as assessee

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm’s length price (Comparability factors - Segmental result) - Assessment year 2008-09 - Whether a company providing medical transcription, medical coding services and application, development and customization services and also engaged in business of developing software products in respect of which segmental data was not available cannot be held comparable to assessee providing ITES services to its AEs - Held, yes [Para 10] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING : A company providing medical transcription, medical coding services and application, development and customization services and also engaged in business of developing software products in respect of which segmental data was not available cannot be held comparable to assessee providing ITES services to its AEs  TRANSFER PRICING : A company who was data analytics KPO service provider and has also acquired another UK based company providing different services, viz., Travel and hospitality cannot be compared to BPO or an IT offshore company such as assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : A company who was KPO providing structural engineering services wherein during year under consideration, extraordinary events such as amalgamation and demerger have taken place cannot be held comparable to assessee  TRANSFER PRICING : A company whose performance of Engineering Design Services is regarded as providing high end services among BPO which requires high skill cannot be held comparable to assessee providing routine low end ITES functions

Section 92C of the Income-tax Act, 1961 - Transfer pricing - Computation of arm's length price (Comparables, functional similarity - Information technology enabled services (ITESs)) - Assessment year 2011-12 - Whether where selected company was engaged in provision of high-end consultancy services, it could not be compared to assessee who was rendering low end IT enabled services - Held, yes [Para 13] [In favour of assessee]TRANSFER PRICING : Where selected company was engaged in provision of high-end consultancy services, it could not be compared to assessee who was providing low end IT enabled services   TRANSFER PRICING : Where assessee is having no working capital risk, then no negative working capital adjustment is called for  TRANSFER PRICING : Where assessee-company was engaged in rendering ITeS, selected company being engaged in business of software development services, contract centre service and IT enabled services, in absence of segmental details, could not be selected as comparable   TRANSFER PRICING : Where selected company was engaged in providing high end services in nature of knowledge process outsourcing (KPO), medical transcriptions, healthcare receivables cycle management and high end consultancy, it could not be compared to assessee engaged in rendering routine low end information technology enabled services  TRANSFER PRICING :Selected company having huge brand value than assessee, could not be accepted as comparable to ITeS provider  TRANSFER PRICING : Where company failed filter of service income being greater than 75 per cent of total revenue and was suffering from huge fluctuations which had influenced its profit margin, it could not be accepted as comparable  TRANSFER PRICING : Where company was engaged in provision of varied services and no segmental breakup of same was available, said company was not comparable to assessee, ITeS provider

ITeS and certain other technical services involving software testing, verification and validation of software, in absence of segmental information, could not be compared with ITES provider  IT/ILT : KPO was incomparable to ITeS segment of assessee

facts.text:
The assessee-company was engaged in providing routine software development (SD) and back office processing services (BPO), pursuant to a single composite contract to its AE for enabling it to service the same to end customers.

The assessee had entered into a single composite agreement/contract' with its AE to provide information technology based services (i.e., software development & support services (SD in short) and Back Office Process Outsourcing (BPO in short) services) on a 'bundled price basis'. Accordingly, the assessee had benchmarked the transaction pertaining to 'rendering of services' using Transactional Net Margin Method (TNMM) as the Most Appropriate Method (MAM) wherein the margin earned by the assessee from 'rendering of services' to AEs was determined to be at 27.50 per cent vis-a-vis 11.44 per cent earned by the comparable companies. Based on the said analysis, the transaction was determined to be at arm's length.

The TPO found from the audited accounts of the assessee company that it had three segments viz. BPO, Software Development and Support. He opined that the profitability from the software segment was at ALP. However, he observed that the profitability of BPO segment was quite low and the comparables for the same were to be determined.

The TPO proceeded to determine the ALP by searching on the Prowess Database the keyword 'ITES', i.e., searching for the comparables only in ITES segment. On the basis of mean margin earned by his own set of comparables, TPO made certain addition to the assessee's ALP.

The DRP agreed to the contention of the assessee it had rendered both SD and ITES services to its AE. The DRP directed the TPO to consider the comparables from IT or SD segment also for arriving at the ALP margin.

On cross appeals:

The assessee-company was engaged in provision of information technology enabled services to both AE's as well as non-AE's.

The assessee applied internal TNMM and compared the OP/OC margin of AE with OP/OC margin of non-AE segment. Since the OP/OC margin of 12.8 per cent in its AE segment was higher than 7.24 per cent OP/OC margin earned in the non-AE segment, it was concluded that the international transaction was at arms' length price.

The TPO proceeded to apply external TNMM to benchmark the said international transaction.

The DRP noted that the nature of services being performed in AE segment was totally different from nature of services in non-AE segment as well as no audited segments were being maintained and the assessee had created artificial segmentation and confirmed T.P.O's order.

On appeal:

The assessee-company was engaged in the business of software development services and ITES/BPO services. The assessee during the year under dispute provided such services only to its Associated Enterprise (AE). It had selected TNM Method as the most appropriate method and OP/TC as the profit level indicator for both the segments.

On reference, the TPO rejected the TP document of the assessee pointing out various defects and deficiencies. He undertook a search in the databases and computed the ALP of both the segments.

On the basis of transfer pricing adjustment computed by the TPO, the Assessing Officer passed the assessment order making certain additions.

The Commissioner (Appeals) dismissed the appeal of the assessee rejecting all its contentions.

The assessee objected to the following companies being treated as comparables in the software service segment:

(i)

Exensys Software Solutions Ltd.: The assessee submitted that not only the aforesaid company was involved in development of products but there was also an extraordinary event of merger during the relevant financial year.

(ii)

Thirdware Solutions Ltd.: The company was into development of product and involved in distribution activities. Therefore, it could not be treated as a comparable.

(iii)

Infosys Technologies Ltd.: The assessee contended that under no circumstances Infosys Technologies Ltd. could be treated as comparable to the assessee as it is a giant in the sector of software development and ITES having considerable brand value. The revenue, on the other hand, while strongly opposing contention of the assessee, submitted that the assessee itself in its own TP Study had selected Infosys Technologies Ltd. as a comparable.

The assessee had also sought exclusion of following comparable companies selected by the TPO in the ITES segment:

(i)

Vishal Information Technologies Ltd.: The company had outsourced a considerable part of its business to third party vendors. That was proved from the fact that only 2 per cent of the revenue was spent towards employee cost and there was huge vendor payment.

(ii)

Maple E Solutions Ltd.: The company could not be treated as comparable as the directors of the said company were found to be involved in fraud, hence financial results of the company could not be trusted as reliable.

(iii)

Wipro BPO Solutions Ltd.: WIPRO commands a premium in the pricing of its products and services due to goodwill, reputation and brand value. Therefore, it could not be compared to a risk mitigated captive service provider like the assessee.

■

The assessee–company was engaged in manufacture, conversion and trading of diversified products and maintained six reportable segments, including a healthcare segment. It applied TNMM for its international transactions in the healthcare segment, earned a margin of 2.90% on sales, and selected five comparables with an arithmetic mean margin of 2.8%, claiming that its segmental results were at arm’s length. The assessee had made payments to its associated enterprise towards administration and business support/IT support services relating to its IT infrastructure. In AY 2008-09, it reported payment of about Rs. 6.12 crores under this head.

■

The TPO rejected the assessee’s study, conducted a fresh search on Prowess and Capitaline, and selected six comparables with an arithmetic mean margin of 14.55% on sales. He retained six comparables and determined margins at 17.10% on OP/OC and 12.22% on OP/Sales for the healthcare segment. He computed arm’s length operating revenue at about Rs. 76.16 crores against actual operating cost of about Rs. 84.25 crores, and proposed a transfer pricing adjustment of about Rs. 8.09 crores under section 92CA. He did not exclude manufacturing companies since, in his view, the assessee also had manufacturing activity and had itself considered a manufacturer (Hicks Thermometer (I) Ltd.) in comparability. The TPO treated the services as intra-group services for which, according to him, the assessee failed to demonstrate rendition and benefit, and applying CUP determined the arm’s length price at Nil, proposing a transfer pricing adjustment of about Rs. 6.12 crores under section 92CA for AY 2008-09.

■

On appeal, the CIT(A) partly allowed the assessee’s appeal. Recording that, as per the assessee’s TP study, trading constituted about 93.1% of sales and conversion/manufacturing about 6.7%, the CIT(A) characterized the assessee’s healthcare segment as predominantly trading. The CIT(A) held Poly Medicure Ltd. to be an exclusively manufacturing-based company (with trading revenue of about 1.39% from inputs) and Opto Circuits (India) Ltd. to have about 91% revenue from manufacturing, and directed exclusion of both from the comparables for the healthcare segment. For AY 2009-10, the CIT(A) directed similar exclusion of Poly Medicure Ltd. and Opto Circuits (India) Ltd. from the comparables on identical grounds. The CIT(A) deleted the adjustment attributable to IT support services, holding that the assessee had paid only maintenance charges for its IT infrastructure (servers, application software and network services, including help desk and disaster recovery/business continuity back-up). The CIT(A) noted that substantial project implementation expenditure of about Rs. 3.89 crores incurred in FY 2004-05 for the IT set-up had already been accepted in AY 2005-06 and, following consistency, accepted the maintenance-related expenditure for the year. For AY 2009-10, the CIT(A) directed acceptance of payment towards IT support services of about Rs. 61.34 lakhs.

■

On appeal to the Tribunal.

The assessee-company was a joint venture between 'T' Group based in Italy and the 'K' Group based in India. The assessee-company was engaged in the activities like EPC lump sum turnkey contracts, engineering design services, supervision services, transaction services and feasibility studies. It also rendered onshore/offshore design and engineering services and field construction supervision services. The assessee-company primarily rendered engineering design services and field construction supervisions services to various entities within the 'T' Group. The trained technical personnel available with the assessee-company were utilised by the 'T' Group for execution of assignments across the globe. The services were rendered either from India or by deputation of personnel of the 'T' offices or at the field construction sites. The assessee-company was compensated on an hourly basis on actual man-hours spent, as captured by time sheets. Therefore, during the year under consideration, it had entered into transactions with its associated enterprises as well as non-associated enterprises. While determining arm's length price, the assessee calculated margin of comparable companies based on segmental data, wherever applicable. The TPO observed that the assessee had provided the split profit & loss account in respect of income from A.Es and non-A.Es. He further pointed out that no authenticated documents were produced to prove the genuineness of split profit and loss account. The segmental accounts were not part of the audited accounts submitted by the assessee. He, therefore, held that the spilt profit and loss account could not be relied on and, accordingly, entity level margin comparison vis-a-vis the comparable companies had to be done. As regard margin of comparable companies considering the segmental data wherever applicable, he accepted the assessee's contention and, accordingly, the margin as provided by the assessee were considered to be the arm's length benchmarks. However, loss making companies were rejected. He also considered the data for financial year 2005-06 only as against for the three years considered by the assessee and computed the arithmetic means at 6.57 per cent in regard to operating profit to operating cost as and computed the adjustments to be made for arriving at arm's length price at Rs. 8,94,37,237. The TPO further pointed out that since the arm's length value of sales/service did not fell within the 5 per cent range, the benefit of proviso to section 92(2) could not be granted to assessee. The Assessing Officer made the adjustments as per the order of the TPO. Against draft assessment order, the assessee filed objections before the Dispute Resolution Panel which were rejected.

On appeal :

The assessee-company rendered software development services and engineering design services to its AE. The assessee had arrived at a set of 6 comparables for its engineering design segment. The average margin of the comparables, using multiple year data was 5.03 per cent. The assessee's margin in this segment was 8.9 per cent. So far as software development segment was concerned, the assessee had arrived at a set of 18 comparables with an average margin of 13.43 per cent. Since the assessee's margin was 21.47 per cent, the transactions were at arm's length price.

The TPO further rejected the assessee's approach of benchmarking engineering design segment and software development segment separately and adopted entity level approach. Accordingly, he undertook a fresh search for comparables and finally selected comparables and determined adjustment.

The Assessing Officer accordingly passed the draft assessment order making upward adjustment.

On appeal:

Assessee, engaged in providing Information Technology Enabled Services (ITES) and software development services, entered into international transactions with its Associated Enterprises. Assessee selected 14 comparables to calculate arithmetic mean and made suo motu transfer pricing adjustment on cost in relation to such services. As assessee's margin was higher than arithmetic mean, assessee claimed its transactions to be at arm's length.

The Transfer Pricing Officer selected 23 comprables and made transfer pricing adjustment. The assessee contended that 'C' could not be taken as a comparable as it outsourced its activities, and that the correct profit of 'M', taken as a comparable by the TPO, had not been determined. It was also contended that segmental profits of 'D' was required to be considered to facilitate comparison. The assessee submitted that if its contentions were accepted, the arithmetic mean would be within the safe harbour of +/- 5 per cent and no adjustment would be required.

On appeal, the Dispute Resolution Panel upheld the order of the Transfer Pricing Officer.

On second appeal:

On the revenue's appeal before the Tribunal:

We have carefully considered submissions of Ld. Representatives of parties and the orders of authorities below. We observe that assessee in the assessment year under consideration is engaged in the business of providing IT enabled services and IT services. The assessee has adopted for both services in determining ALP TNMM method. The assessee while making TP study for determining ALP has 14 companies as comparable in respect of IT Enabled services segment and 22 companies comparable in respect of IT services segment and arrived at arithmetic means at 9.59 per cent and 10.24 per cent respectively as against 19.73 per cent of assessee's operating margin for IT enabled services and 23 per cent for IT services. However, TPO while making its TP study aggregated both segments. TPO considered functionality of 14 comparable companies furnished by assessee in respect of its IT enabled services and out of it he found 8 companies as comparable and rejected the balance 6 companies as not comparable. Since TPO found that 8 comparable companies provided in TPO report of assessee were inadequate in number, he took 25 set of comparable companies for IT enabled services . It is relevant to state that out of 25 set of those companies, 3 companies are common with assessee's own set of comparables. Assessee disputed 21 companies out of 25 comparable companies considered by department and filed objections before TPO as well as before DRP. TPO considered ALP of assessee's international transaction with associated enterprises by adopting arithmetic mean of 27.84 per cent and suggested upward adjustment of Rs. 9,29,93,816, after rejecting the objections of assessee. DRP in its order passed under section 144C(5) confirmed adjustment suggested by TPO with the direction to AO to give working capital adjustment by following decision of DRP in assessee's own case for assessment year 2006-07. As mentioned herein above, AO made assessment under section 143(3), read with section 144C but did not comply with direction of DRP to give working capital adjustment and stated that relevant details of comparables to give working capital adjustment is required and it also requires an exhaustive exercise before giving working capital adjustment.

During the course of hearing, the assessee disputed functionality, assets and risk of 7 companies as not comparable out of 30 comparable cases considered by TPO to arrive at arithmetic means of 27.84 per cent with the assessee company. The assessee submitted that actual margin of all 30 comparable companies considered by TPO is 26.5 per cent as per their annual reports. The Revenue did not dispute said contention of assessee and submitted that this could be verified by AO while giving effect to order of ITAT.

The assessee-company was engaged in activities like EPC lump sum turnkey contracts, engineering design services, supervision services, translation services and feasibility studies. During the year in question, it rendered services to 'T' group concerns through its personnel either from India or by deputation at the 'T' office or at the construction site. The assessee had a fully owned subsidiary called ICB. This company received revenues from its AE, JTS to the tune of Rs. 26.26 crore, which constituted 59 per cent of its total revenues. The assessee computed Arm's Length Price by using Transactional Net Margin Method using Profit Level Indicator as Operating profit to Cost. In its transfer pricing study, the assessee chose twelve cases as comparable giving average margin of operating profit to cost at 15.37 per cent. The assessee declared that its margin from international transactions with AEs at 75.48 per cent on cost was better than the average profit margin on similar base of twelve comparable cases shown by it. The Assessing Officer made a reference to the Transfer Pricing Officer under section 92CA(1). The TPO took a view that, (i) twelve cases considered by the assessee as comparable were functionally different on end level and, hence, should be excluded for benchmarking. (ii ) ICB was an internally comparable case which had earned 66.77 per cent profit margin over total cost. It was only this cost which should be considered for determining ALP in assessee's case. (iii ) The assessee's contention that ICB had related party transactions of Rs. 29.53 crore including Rs. 26.26 crore as receipts from JTS and, hence, the same be excluded as controlled transactions, was not acceptable. The TPO thus adopted net profit margin over cost at 66.77 per cent for determining ALP in respect of the payments received by the assessee from its AEs and resultantly proposed adjustment of Rs. 7.13 crore (after rectification). On appeal, the Commissioner (Appeals) held that (a) the TPO was wrong in rejecting all the twelve comparable cases cited by the assessee on entity level. Ten cases out of such twelve were functionally comparable on segment level. (b) ICB was functionally different inasmuch as it entered into the project business executing various electrical and instrumentation projects while the assessee's international transactions were in relation to service segment. (c) Transactions of ICB with JTS constituted related party transactions and, hence, the case of ICB should be excluded from the comparable cases. (d) On the basis of remaining ten comparable cases, the assessee's transactions with its AEs and its margin on cost at 75.48 per cent or even 44.21 per cent, was at arm's length and hence no addition was warranted. The Accountant Member in his opinion held that JTS was AE of ICB and, hence, the transactions between them constituted (d) controlled transactions. In that view of the matter, he ruled out the case ICB for determining the ALP in respect of the assessee's international transactions. It was further held that the Commissioner (Appeals) was justified in accepting ten out of twelve cases considered by the assessee in its transfer pricing study as comparable because the assessee had given segmental data whereas the TPO rejected these cases due to non-comparability at the entity level. He, therefore, declined to interfere with the view of the Commissioner (Appeals) in this regard, thereby dismissing the appeal of the Revenue. On the other hand, the Judicial Member did not agree with the reasons as well as finding of the Accountant Member on the issue of internal comparable. The sum and substance of his finding was that when a transaction with AE was found and accepted at ALP, then such comparable transaction could also be considered for determining ALP in respect of other cases having transactions with its AEs. By applying this logic to the present situation, he opined that since the transactions between ICB and JTS were found to be at ALP, there was no reason to ignore such internally comparable transaction for determining ALP in respect of the assessee's international transactions. He held that the contrary view of the Commissioner (Appeals) on this issue, as upheld by the Accountant Member, was not sustainable. In view of difference of opinion between the two Members of the Tribunal, the matter was referred to the Third Member.

[Para 37]

It is noted from records that the DRP in assessee's own case in assessment year 2009-10 has directed the TPO to delete Coral Hub Ltd. from the final set of comparable with the observation that this company is outsourcing its activity whereas the assessee does not outsource. Therefore, the business modal of the assessee is different. [Para 9]

Further in the case of Mercer Consulting (India) (P.) Ltd. v. Dy. CIT [2014] 150 ITD 1/47 taxmann.com 84 (Delhi - Trib.) for assessment year 2009-10, held that the Coral Hub Ltd. was not includable in the list of comparable because of major outsourcing and therefore, the same was required to be excluded from the list of comparables for measuring arm's length price of the ITES segmental transactions. [Para 10]

In view of above, it is opined that the outsourcing charges, which constitute more than 90 per cent of the total operating cost of the Coral Hub Ltd., is a very important factor and the same having greater bearing on the profitability of the comparable. In this situation, the Coral Hub Ltd. cannot be considered as a suitable comparable for benchmarking of International transactions of the assessee in ITES segmental activities, because the factum of heavy outsourcing activity carried out by this company looses the tag of suitable comparability. Since, the facts of the present case are similar to the facts of assessment year 2009-10, wherein the DRP itself did not find the Coral Hub Ltd. as a suitable comparable in the assessee company, therefore, following the view taken by Tribunal Delhi 'I' Bench in the case of Mercer Consulting (India) (P.) Ltd. (supra) it is held that Coral Hub Ltd. deserves to be excluded from the final list of comparables. [Para 11]

Eclerx Services Ltd.

It is noted that the Eclerx Services Ltd. is engaged in providing data analytics and customized process to its host of global clients which also provides services to the banking, manufacturing, retail, travel and hospitability business entities. DRP has not disputed this fact that the ITES segmental solutions offered by it also include data analytics operation management, audit and reconciliation, metrics management and reporting services. Apparently, this company provides tailored process outsourcing and management services in addition to multitude of the data aggregation, and mining and maintenance services. From annual report available on record, it can be easily seen that it is not closed to the assessee ITES segmental services transaction which are impressed by the manual process ITES services. The conclusion of the DRP that no comparable can be excluded on the ground of abnormal margin if its functionally comparable to the tested party cannot be accepted because mergers/demergers bring exceptional financial result which make such company as unfit for comparison. In view of foregoing discussion, it is held that the Eclerx Services Ltd. is not a suitable comparable to the assessee company for assessment year 2008-09 due to high pitched financial result and the same deserve to be deleted from the final set of comparables. [Para 15]

Cosmic Global Ltd.

Merely because the assessee company included this company in the list of comparables, the functionally different company cannot be accepted at suitable comparables. When the assessee is claiming that the Cosmic Global Ltd. was included due to in advertent mistake in the set of comparables proposed by the assessee then this bona fide act of the assessee cannot be a reason to prohibit the assessee from claiming and contending that it was included by mistake. The Revenue authorities and the Tribunal has to see that whether the company is, in fact, functionally comparable or not. The objection to the inclusion of a particular comparable cannot be rejected at threshold only because the same was included by the assessee under a bona fide mistake in the list of proposed comparable. [Para 17]

While considering the functionally comparability of Cosmic Global services with the assessee company, it is found that the Tribunal in its order in the case of United Health Group Information Services (P.) Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2014] 151 ITD 556/50 taxmann.com 177 (Delhi) wherein for the same Assessment year 2008-09 held that the major part of income from this company comes from translation charges which is amounting to Rs. 5.59 crores out of total revenues of Rs. 5.86 crores, which is totally dissimilar to that of the assessee of that case.

The nature of services rendered by the assessee to non-AEs broadly comprised of customer care and technical support, viz., payroll, recruitment, IT support etc. The business operations of the assessee are divided into various operational processes that it performs for its customers (AE's and non - AE's). While processes carried out for the AE and non-AE may differ, the fundamental functions performed by the assessee under each of these processes are the same and fall under the category of ITeS Industry. These aspects were never disputed by the TPO/AO at any stage. In fact, the TPO/AO simply stated that the nature of services performed in AE segment are totally different from nature of services in non-AE segment. But how the services are fundamentally different has not been demonstrated by the Assessing Officer. In fact, in broader context the services rendered to AE and non-AE were that of customer care and technical support, and thus, rejecting the internal TNMM on this ground was not valid as internal TNMM is the method which makes it easy to find comparable companies and reasonably determine the arm's length nature of related as well as unrelated transactions. Besides this the TPO/AO has also rejected internal TNMM on the ground that there were no audited segments maintained. But at the same time, the TPO/AO has not pointed out any discrepancy related to segmental analysis based on valid allocation keys furnished by the assessee in its TP study. Therefore, these two aspects cannot be valid for rejecting the internal TNMM. The DRP was not correct in considering the services/scope of work from the agreement entered into by the assessee with its AE for 'procurement of IT Services' and comparing the same with the back-end ITeS services provided by the assessee to AEs. In the present case, best suited method is internal TNMM. The financial data pertaining to internal segmentation is more reliable and accurate, as compared to financial data of external comparable companies, therefore, it will be appropriate to apply internal benchmarking analysis over external benchmarking analysis. The "OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises and Tax Administrations" highlight the preference of internal comparables over external comparables. In fact, the United Nations Practical Manual on Transfer Pricing for Developing Countries, released in 2013 (UN manual) also provides that TNMM is less dependent on product comparability because net margins are less influenced by differences in products and functions, as compared to other methods like CUP. Therefore, the TPO/AO is directed adopt internal TNMM for benchmarking provision of ITeS. [Para 10]

Wipro Technology Services Ltd.

Functionally Not Comparable: It is found that the selected company, which is primarily engaged in providing information technology software solutions, provides diversified services comprising software related support services, primarily information technology software solutions/maintenance and technology support services, unlike the assessee which is engaged in Information technology services only.

Non-availability of segmental accounts: It is found from a perusal of the 'Annual report' of this company that no segmental information is available as regards the IT software solutions/maintenance and technology infrastructure support services provided by the aforesaid company. Said company was engaged in providing software related support services, primarily information technology software solutions/maintenance and technology support services to Citigroup entities, which is considered as one segment, and, therefore, no reportable segments are available.

Significant related party transactions: The coordinate bench of the Tribunal in the case of Saxo India (P.) Ltd. v. Asstt. CIT [2016] 67 taxmann.com 155 (Delhi-Trib.)while disposing of the appeal of the assessee before it, had excluded the selected company as a comparable on the ground that the latter had significant related party transactions pursuant to its master services agreement with the Citigroup Inc. The Tribunal observed that the holding company, i.e. Wipro Ltd. had acquired all the interests held by Citigroup Inc. in Citi Technology Services Ltd. (subsequently renamed as Wipro Technology Services Ltd.). That thereafter Wipro Ltd. (supra) had entered into a master service agreement with Citigroup Inc. for providing technology infrastructure services and application development services for a period of six years. Thus, it was observed by the Tribunal that income from software development support and maintenance services were earned by Wipro Technology Services Ltd., from Citi Group Inc., by means of matter service agreement entered into between Wipro Ltd., and Citi Group Inc., a third person. It was further observed by the Tribunal that Wipro technology was engaged in providing IT software solutions/maintenance and technology infrastructure support services to Citi Group entities globally, and as the services rendered by Wipro Technology to Citi Group was determined by Wipro Limited and Citigroup Inc., therefore, the entities to whom services were rendered became deemed associate enterprises, and accordingly, the transactions of rendering of services were to be construed as deemed international transactions as per section 92B(2), and, thus, the Citi group was to be construed as an associated enterprise of Wipro Technology. Thus, the Tribunal is correct as regards substantial related party transactions in the case of the aforesaid company, as a fall out of which the same could not have been taken as a comparable as against the assessee. [Para 18]

Thus, when the said company is functionally not comparable with the assessee-company; its segmental details are not available, and has substantial related party transactions, therefore, it can safely be concluded that the said company had wrongly been included by the TPO as a comparable. [Para 19]

USA which has led to rapid increase in its customer base. Such acquisition definitely has an impact on the trading result and can distort profit margin. Comparable Global Ltd.

The assessee has sought exclusion of this comparable company mainly on the ground that it outsources most of its work which is 57.31 per cent as compared to the assessee which is only 2.5 per cent and employee cost of this company is lower. Though this is fairly a vital factor vitiating the comparability, however, the assessee could not give any rebuttal or any cogent reasons as to why this comparable company was selected and chosen by the assessee after carrying out FAR analysis not only in earlier years, but also in subsequent assessment years i.e. 2010-11 and 2011-12 again on carrying same FAR analysis. It is only in this year that assessee is seeking exclusion on the ground that it has a different business model. Such pick and choose of comparables every year according to the suitability of the margin definitely amounts to cherry picking. The assessee has not demonstrated that in earlier years and subsequent years the business model of Cosmic Global Ltd. is different, i.e., it does not outsource its substantial work. No doubt assessee can object to inclusion or exclusion of a comparable company contrary to its TP Study Report by citing cogent grounds and pointing out the factors vitiating the comparability and TPO has to examine these comparability factors on merits, but when assessee consistently adopts any comparable company and too after FAR scrutiny then onus is very heavy upon the assessee to substantiate that the material factors in the relevant year are different from the years when it seeks to take contrary stand in a particular year. The assessee has been unable to point out the material factors for distinction sought in this year was not permeating in the earlier years or in the subsequent years. This inconsistent approach cannot be permitted as it can lead to falling in the realm of whims of suitability of assessee. Had it been the case where material facts were different in this year and the comparable has been selected on some incorrect analysis in the earlier year or at the time of TP study, then definitely there cannot be any estoppel for objecting to for exclusion, but such material facts and incorrect approach has to be demonstrated which has not been done in this year. This inconsistency is further accentuated by the fact that this comparable continues to be part of assessee's comparable in subsequent years. Thus, assessee cannot be allowed to resort to such cherry picking. Accordingly, the action of the TPO in including Cosmic Global Ltd. as comparable following rule of consistency is upheld. [Para 15.3]

Comparable E-Clerex Services Ltd.

This company due to its exceptional performance during the year, has been chosen as best KPO company and it has also outsourced its substantial work to the third party during the year. The assessee on the other hand is providing back office support services and such services are being provided by its own human resources, that is, it is not outsourcing its work. It is the trite law that it is not necessary to take the comparable used in one year for working out the ALP of the assessee in the subsequent year. It is for the reason that the determination of ALP depends upon various factors which keep on changing year after year. [Para 51.10]

In view of the above, it is to be held that no adverse inference can be drawn against the assessee merely on the reasoning that the impugned comparable has been used in the earlier year while working out the ALP of the assessee for the international transaction carried out with the AE until and unless all the facts and circumstances for both years remain unchanged. [Para 51.11]

Coming to the case on hand, the entire basis of the allegation of the TPO for using the impugned comparable while working out the ALP of the assessee was based on the information gathered in response to the notice issued under section 133(6). Admittedly, such information was supplied to the assessee by the revenue. However, the assessee has pointed out certain glaring facts having adverse impact about the report supplied by the revenue it. None of the authorities below has clarified those allegations of the assessee but merely proceeded to use the information gathered in response to the notice issued under section 133(6) as the gospel truth. Thus, what is transpired that neither the opportunity to the assessee was afforded nor points highlighted by the assessee in the financials of the BPO segment were addressed. Thus, in such facts and circumstances, it is of the view that the information gathered by the revenue in response to the notice issued under section 133(6) cannot be used while working out the ALP of the assessee. Coral Hub Ltd.

This case was earlier included by the assessee in the list of comparables in the transfer pricing study by considering multiple-year data. However, when the TPO required the assessee to furnish data of comparables for the current year alone, the assessee requested for the exclusion of this case from the list of comparables. The revenue opposed this contention by urging that the assessee cannot be allowed to resile from its original stand. [Para 12.1] The legal objection taken by the revenue that the assessee should be prohibited from taking a stand contrary to the one which was taken at the stage of the TP study or during the course of proceedings before the authorities below cannot be accepted. It goes without saying that the object of assessment is to determine the income in respect of which the assessee is rightly chargeable to tax. As the income not originally offered for taxation, if otherwise chargeable, is required to be included in the total income, in the same breath, any income wrongly included in the total income, which is not otherwise chargeable, should be excluded. There can be no estoppel against the provisions of the Act. Extending this proposition further to the context of the transfer pricing, if the assessee fails to report an otherwise comparable case, then the TPO is obliged to include it in the list of comparables, and in the same manner, if the assessee wrongly reported an incomparable case as comparable in its TP study and then later on claims that it should be excluded then, there should be nothing to forbid the assessee from claiming so, provided the TPO is satisfied that the case so originally reported as comparable is, in fact, not comparable. [Para 12.2]

The material on record suggests that outsourcing charges of comparable constitute 90 per cent of the total operating cost in this case.
